# (Dolmas)

BEST Stuffed Grape Leaves (Dolmas) - The Mediterranean Dish

## Overview
- **Prep Time**: 45 mins Cook Time
- **Cook Time**: 60 mins Method
- **Total Time**: 1 hour 45 minutes Yield
- **Servings**: 1

## Ingredients
- 1 16-oz jar grape leaves in brine (about 60 to 70 leaves), I used Oralndo brand (affiliate link)
- 1 1/2 cup short grain rice, soaked in plenty of water for 15 minutes, then drained
- Extra virgin olive oil (I used Private Reserve Greek EVOO)
- 1 large yellow onion, finely chopped
- 12 oz lean ground beef
- Kosher salt
- Black pepper
- 1 tsp allspice
- 1/2 tsp cumin
- 1/2 cup EACH chopped fresh parsley, fresh dill, and fresh mint
- 1 to 2 tomatoes sliced into rounds
- About 4 cups or more low-sodium chicken broth or water
- Juice of 2 lemons
- Cook Mode Prevent your screen from going dark
- 1/5
- BEST Stuffed Grape Leaves (Dolmas) - The Mediterranean Dish

## Instructions
1. Prepare the Grape Leaves
1. If using jarred grape leaves as I am here, remove them from the jar and discard the brine. Rinse the grape leaves well and place
2. them in a colander to drain. (Later in the process, you'll remove the stems before stuffing.) (See notes if using fresh grape leaves)
3. Prepare the Stuffing
1. Soak the rice in plenty of water for about 15 to 20 minutes or until you are able to break one grain of rice easily. Drain well.
2. While the rice is soaking, cook the meat. Heat 1 tbsp extra virgin olive oil in a large skillet. Add onions and cook briefly, about 2
3. minutes or so, tossing until translucent. Add the meat and cook till fully browned, tossing occasionally. Drain any excess fat, then
4. season the meat with kosher salt, pepper, and spices. Toss to combine. Remove from heat and set aside to cool.
3. In a mixing bowl, combine the meat, drained rice, and fresh herbs. Season lightly with kosher salt. Add a generous drizzle of extra
4. virgin olive oil, and mix so that everything is well-incorporated.
5. Stuff Grape Leaves, Assemble, and Cook
1. Prepare a heavy cooking pot and lightly brush the bottom with extra virgin olive oil. Arrange a few grape leaves in the bottom (I
2. used the leaves that didn't look too great here and made three layers to protect the stuffed leaves from scorching later.) Top with
3. sliced tomatoes.
2. To stuff the grape leaves, you will work one leaf at a time. Place one grape leave on a cutting board the textured/rough side facing
3. you. Take 1 heaping teaspoon of the filling and place in the center of the leave, then fold the sides over the filling and roll (think
4. about this like rolling spring rolls or cigars.) Repeat with the remaining grape leaves or until you're out of stuffing.
3. Neatly arrange the grape leaves in row, seam side down, in your prepared pot, covering the circumference of the pot. Then place
4. a small plate inverted on top. Boil the broth or water and pour over the grape leaves, arriving at the top layer and somewhat
5. covering (about 4 cups liquid, maybe a little more.)
4. Now cover the pot with the lid and cook over medium heat for 30 minutes until the liquid has been absorbed. Uncover and
5. remove the plate, then pour juice of 2 lemons. Cover again with the lid (no need for the plate at this point), cook on low heat for
6. 30 to 45 more minutes or until fully cooked.
7. BEST Stuffed Grape Leaves (Dolmas) - The Mediterranean Dish
8. To Serve
1. Remove grape leaves from heat. Allow to rest uncovered for 20 to 30 minutes before serving.
2. Add a generous drizzle of quality extra virgin olive oil (I used Private Reserve EVOO), and transfer to a serving platter.
3. Serve with a side of Greek Tzatziki sauce or plain yogurt and wedges of lemon. (More suggestions for what to serve along in the
4. post above)

## Notes
Cooks Tips for Best Results: 1) Be sure to soak the rice before using, this allows it cook well and more evenly. 2) Don't over-stuff the
grape leaves, remember that the filling is mostly of rice and it will expand as it cooks. 3) Roll the grape leaves tightly enough so that
they don't unravel or become undone while cooking, BUT again, remember rice will expand as it cooks, so don't fold too tightly or
the rice won't cook properly. 4) Adding a small inverted plate on top of assembled grape leaves in the pot helps keep them intact
and in place and prevents them from floating while cooking. Once the liquid has been absorbed, you can remove the plate to finish
cooking as instructed. 5) Once cooked, allow the grape leaves to rest for 20 to 30 minutes so that any remaining liquids are absorbed
and the leaves set nicely, plus they just taste better.
Vegetarian Option:The difference in vegetarian grape leaves is obviously in the stuffing mixture. You will need to omit the meat and
add 1/2 cup more rice. Sautee the onions (no meat this time) until translucent. And add onions to the rice. Add spices (allspice and
cumin) and pinch of salt and add the fresh herbs. Mix to combine and use this vegetarian mixture in the recipe as outlined.
If using fresh grape leaves: wash them very well and blanch them in boiling hot water. Remove from water using a slotted spoon
and place them in a colander to fully cool and drain.
Leftovers: Store properly in the fridge in a tight-lid, refrigerator-safe container for 3 to 4 days. You can enjoy them cold or reheat. To
reheat, place in a pot with a tiny bit of liquid, cover and heat over medium-low heat until warmed through.
Prepare-Ahead Tips: 1) You can prepare the stuffing 1 to 2 nights in advance and keep refrigerated in a tight-lid glass container in
the fridge. 2) You can also roll the grape leaves and assemble them fully up to 1 night in advance and keep refrigerated until ready to
cook. I like to take them out of the fridge for a bit before cooking so they are not so cold.

WILD RECIPES By: The wild Bunch
At wildbrine, we love to incorporate sauerkraut into some of our favorite classic recipes for an unexpected twist of texture
and �avor. Looking for some ideas on how to add this probiotic powerhouse to your own culinary regimen? Read on to
discover our 20 favorite uses for sauerkraut. Have a favorite of your own? Share in the comments!
Tips for Cooking with Sauerkraut
Sauerkraut naturally lends itself to recipes that call for pickles, olives, or other briny ingredients. Keep this in mind
when brainstorming your own uses for sauerkraut.
Preserve sauerkraut’s bene�cial bacteria by keeping its temperature below 115 degrees F.
Sauerkraut brine is also a versatile ingredient and can be used in recipes such as salad dressings, cocktails, or sauces.
(Be sure to keep enough brine in the jar to cover the vegetables, as this helps keep it fresh.)
Our Favorite Uses for Sauerkraut
1. Tuna salad: Love dill pickle relish in your tuna salad? For extra zip, try chopped sauerkraut instead.
2. Deviled eggs: Minced sauerkraut could be the new secret ingredient to your deviled eggs. Here’s a recipe where we
use kimchi, but you can substitute kraut.
3. Grilled cheese: Elevate your grilled cheese sandwich with the addition of sauerkraut.
4. Baked potato: Potatoes and sauerkraut are a Bavarian favorite. We like to top baked potatoes with sour cream
and our Dill Garlic Sauerkraut.
5. Fish tacos: Brighten your traditional �sh tacos by topping them with sauerkraut instead of plain cabbage. Cilantro
and chipotle crema also highly recommended!
6. Cubano sandwich: Sauerkraut stands in for pickles in this classic pressed sandwich of ham, Swiss cheese, and
mustard.
7. Potato salad: Sauerkraut is an appealing addition to both classic and German potato salad. Give it a try at your
next gathering.
8. Egg salad: Add new dimension and crunch to classic egg salad with the addition of sauerkraut.
9. Bagel and lox: Sauerkraut adds a caper-like zing to a bagel with smoked salmon and cream cheese.
10. Cheese plate: Sauerkraut seamlessly stands in for olives or pickles on an artisan cheese plate. Try pairing it with
aged gouda and some crusty bread.
11. Avocado toast: Whole grain bread, sliced avocado, and sauerkraut could become your new favorite avocado toast.
12. Burgers: Hamburgers and meatless burgers are guaranteed to sing with the addition of sauerkraut and melted
swiss cheese.
13. Coleslaw: Sauerkraut and coleslaw are practically cousins. Let them hang out by combining �ve parts shredded
cabbage to one part sauerkraut and refrigerating for at least 30 minutes. Want something fancier? Our recipe for
Sauerkraut Slaw.

14. Sushi: Looking for a unique accompaniment to sushi? Try our Arame Ginger Kraut instead of traditional pickled
ginger
15. Dirty sauerkraut martini: Combine 6 oz vodka, 1 oz sauerkraut brine, and a dash of vermouth for a fun twist on the
dirty martini. Prefer tequila? Here’s another sauerkraut-brine based cocktail recipe.
16. Breakfast burrito: Instead of salsa, add zippy sauerkraut to your next breakfast burrito of eggs, cheese, and
sausage
17. Sandwich or wrap: Give your favorite hand-held meal (with turkey and avocado, hummus and veggies, roast beef
and Swiss cheese) an extra kick with addition of sauerkraut. You will NOT be disappointed.
18. Salad: Pack even more nutritional power into your next Buddha bowl or Superfood Salad with the addition of
sauerkraut.
19. Soup: Garnish potato leek soup with a dollop of sour cream or crème frâiche and a smattering of sauerkraut.
20. One of our favorite uses for sauerkraut: Eat it right out of the jar

# 4-Ingredient Gluten Free Sourdough Bread Recipe - What the Fork

4-Ingredient Gluten Free Sourdough Bread Recipe - What the Fork

## Overview
- **Prep Time**: 5 MINUTES cook time
- **Cook Time**: 1 HOUR 20 MINUTES additional time
- **Total Time**: 21 HOURS 25 MINUTES servings
- **Servings**: 1 LOAF by

## Ingredients
- 200 grams un-fed Gluten-Free Sourdough Starter see notes
- 420 grams Bob's Red Mill 1:1 Gluten-Free Baking Flour see note 10
- 300 grams bottled water cold or room temperature
- 12 grams fine sea salt

## Instructions
1. Day 1 (Around 12 pm)
1. Make the dough: Add the un-fed starter, gluten-free flour, water, and salt to the bowl of a
2. stand mixer. Use the dough hook to mix until all ingredients are combined, the dough
3. comes together, and there isn't any loose flour left.
2. Bulk Fermentation: Gently form the dough into a ball and place in a lightly oiled and
3. floured medium glass bowl. Loosely cover and leave in a draft-free place for 6-10 hours.
4. 6 hours if your house is on the warm side and up to 10 hours if your house is cooler. I
5. generally let mine rise for about 8 hours. At this point, you don't want your dough to
6. double in size.
3. 2nd Proof/Retard (around 8pm): After the first rise, transfer the bowl to the refrigerator to
4. finish proofing in the refrigerator for 12 hours. You can keep the dough in the same bowl
5. or you can gently reshape it and place it in a floured Banneton Basket.
6. 4-Ingredient Gluten Free Sourdough Bread Recipe - What the Fork
7. Day 2 (Around 8 am)
1. Place your Dutch Oven on the center rack and preheat the oven to 500 degrees. Let the
2. Dutch Oven preheat at 500 degrees for at least 30 minutes.
2. When the Dutch Oven has preheated, remove from the dough from the refrigerator. Turn
3. the dough out onto a piece of lightly floured parchment paper.
3. With generously floured hands, gently re-shape to a tighter ball and use the flour to
4. smooth the dough. The dough should be completely coated with a layer of flour. (Skip
5. this if you proofed in a Banneton Basket)
4. Use a sharp knife or bread lame to slash the bread, you want the slash to be at least 1-
5. inch deep. You can make it decorative or keep it simple to start and just do an X in the
6. middle.
5. Remove the Dutch Oven from the preheated oven. Use the corners of the parchment
6. paper to lift the dough and carefully place it in the Dutch Oven so you don't burn
7. yourself. Place 2 large ice cubes in the Dutch Oven between the parchment paper and
8. sides of the DO and quickly cover with the lid.
6. Place the Dutch Oven back on the center rack and lower the temperature to 450 degrees.
7. Bake at 450 for 40 minutes.
7. After 40 minutes lower the oven temperature to 425 degrees and then remove the lid
8. from the Dutch Oven. Bake for an additional 40 minutes, uncovered, at 425 degrees.
8. When the bread is done, it should have an internal temperature of at least 210 degrees
9. and the bottom of the bread should sound hollow when you knock on it. Cool
10. completely on a wire rack before slicing and serving.

## Notes
1. The sourdough starter used and tested in this recipe is made with Bob's Red Mill 1:1
Gluten-Free Baking Flour. It's a 100% hydration starter, which means it's made with equal
parts flour and water.
2. The flour blend I use contains xanthan gum. For best results use the flour listed in the
recipe or another high-quality gluten-free flour blend that already contains xanthan gum.
3. Tap water can be subbed as long as it hasn't been chemically treated. Chlorine will kill the
active cultures and wild yeast.
4. This dough can be mixed by hand if you don't have a stand mixer. I use a Danish Dough
Whisk to mix it.
5. The sourdough bread process is not the same as traditional sourdough bread made with
wheat flour. There's no stretching or folding of the dough during the bulk fermentation.
With gluten-free dough, the bulk fermentation is just the first rise.
6. I finish proofing the dough in the refrigerator, sometimes referred to as Retard. It slows
down the rise and helps prevent over-proofing your dough.
7. I use a 5.5 quart Dutch Oven to bake this bread. If you don't have a Dutch Oven, you can
use a cast-iron skillet and cover the bread with aluminum foil for the 1st half of the
baking process. Be careful not to burn yourself when covering with foil.
8. It's important to cool the bread completely before slicing.
9. This bread is best served toasted. Think toast for breakfast, garlic bread, etc.
 2/4

10. To make this bread with a flour blend that doesn't contain xanthan gum, mix 15g whole
Psyllium Husk with the water and let it sit until it gels. Then mix the ingredients and
follow the directions as indicated.

# A Great Pork Chop Marinade

A Great Pork Chop Marinade - RecipeTin Eats

## Overview
- **Total Time**: 5 mins 10 mins 15 mins
- **Servings**: 4

## Ingredients
- 4 bone in pork chops, 2 cm / 4/5" thick about 280g/9 oz each (Note 1)
- 1 tbsp oil

**Marinade:**
- 1/3 cup (85 ml) soy sauce (light or all purpose, not dark)
- 2 tbsp brown sugar
- 2 tsp Worcestershire sauce
- 1 tsp Dijon mustard
- 2 garlic cloves , minced
- ¼ tsp black pepper

## Instructions
1. Place Marinade ingredients in a ziplock bag. Massage to combine.
2. Add chops. Massage to coat in the Marinade. Marinate for 1 – 24 hours. (Note 2)
3. Take the chops out of the fridge 20 minutes before cooking.
4. Brush BBQ grill or drizzle oil in pan, heat on medium high. Add pork and cook for 4 minutes
5. or until the underside is caramelised and the pork releases from the grill, then turn the chops
6. and cook for 3 minutes (Note 2 for thin chops).
5. Baste both sides with residual marinade in ziplock bag, then cook the basted side for 30
6. seconds before serving. The chops should have a great crust
6. Transfer chops to a plate, cover loosely with foil. Rest for 3 minutes before serving.

## Notes
1. Chops: I used thick, bone in pork chops that were just under 2.5cm / 1" thick. On the bone,
slightly trimmed but not much, I like keeping some fat on the edges to keep the pork really juicy!
This recipe will work with any quick cook cut of pork - chops, steaks, even tenderloin.
2. Minimum marinade time: * Thin chops: 1.25 cm/ 1/2" thick - 1 hr+ * Thick chops 2 cm / 4/5"
thick - 3 hrs+
 1/2
 A Great Pork Chop Marinade - RecipeTin Eats
COOK TIME for just white (juicy, no pink, reduce by 1 min for hint of blush): * Thin chops - 3
minutes first side, 2 minutes second side, then 30 seconds on each side for basting. * Thick chops -
4 minutes first side, 3 minutes second side, then 45 seconds on each side.
If your chops are thicker than the Thick Chops, then I'd recommend starting on the stove and
finishing in the oven at 180C/350F until the internal temperature is 145F / 63C.
3. Troubleshooting / tips: Once you put the chops on the BBQ, DON'T TOUCH IT! Once it is
cooked, it will release naturally from the grills. If it sticks, it's not ready to turn. If your chops are
cooking too quickly and start to burn because of the sugar in the marinade, turn the heat down.
Remember, these chops are meant to have a gorgeous chargrilled crust!
4. CRISPY POTATO ROSTI recipe (pictured on the side of the chops) - by reader request, here's an
abbreviated form of the recipe: 2 large brushed (Sebago) potatoes (US: use russet), peeled and
grated using a box grater. Grab handfuls and squeeze out excess liquid or do this using a dish
towel (clean!). Place in bowl, sprinkle generously with salt and pepper. Melt 1 tbsp butter + 1 1/2
tbsp oil (I use olive) in a large skillet over medium high heat. Add dollops of potato, spread into
pancake shape about 12 cm / 4.5" wide, 0.75 cm / 1/4" thick. Press down to compact into rosti,
cook for 3 minutes or until deep golden brown. Flip and repeat. Drain on paper towels, repeat with
remaining potato, should make 8.
Originally posted August 2017, photos replaced in May 2018, some tidying up done in February
2019, no change to recipe.

Aloo Gobi
By Naz Deravian
Updated Jan. 2, 2024
Total Time 1 hour 10 minutes
Prep Time 10 minutes

Rating (768)
Wonderfully fragrant and loaded with flavor thanks to garam masala, coriander and ground cumin as well as the mild heat of Kashmiri red
chiles, this South Asian potato and cauliflower curry can be served as a vegetarian main or side dish. Preparation of aloo gobi (its name
means “potatoes cauliflower”) can vary, but the one constant is that the vegetables must be cooked until tender but not falling apart. Some
recipes call for deep-frying the vegetables first, while others roast or boil them; here, theyʼre partially sautéed, then finished by steaming, so
everything is done in one pan. Tomatoes arenʼt always typical in aloo gobi, but they add extra moisture and acidity to the dish. This version
skews toward the drier side, so add just enough water to help the vegetables finish steaming. For a little tang, sprinkle on some amchur
(dried mango powder), or drizzle with lemon juice. Serve aloo gobi with roti, or basmati rice and naan.

Take a pastry rectangle and place it with the long side facing you on a flat work surface.

sheet will form an equilateral triangle with sides that are about 3 inches long. This triangle
will be the final shape and size of the samosa. Fold the triangle so its right outer edge is
aligned with the horizontal bottom edge of the sheet. There should now be a triangular
pocket with two flaps sticking out to the left. Pick up the pocket so it is open and upright

pan and arrange them on the pan in a single layer in rows. Bake, turning once halfway
through, until evenly golden brown, 6 to 8 minutes per side. Transfer to a cooling rack or
plate lined with a paper towel to prevent them from getting soggy.

Serve hot or warm with the mint chutney for dipping.

about three times the length of the short sides.

# Baba Ganoush Recipe

Baba Ganoush Recipe - The Mediterranean Dish

## Overview
- **Total Time**: 15 mins 20 mins time 35 mins
- **Servings**: 6 or more people Calories

## Ingredients
- 2 Italian eggplants or small globe eggplants
- ¼ cup tahini paste I used Soom tahini
- 1 lemon, juice of
- 1 garlic clove, minced
- 1 tablespoon plain Greek yogurt, optional
- Kosher salt and black pepper
- 1 teaspoon sumac
- ¾ teaspoon Aleppo pepper or red pepper flakes, optional
- Extra virgin olive oil
- Toasted pine nuts for garnish, optional

## Instructions
1. First, smoke or grill the eggplant. Turn one gas burner on medium-high. Place the eggplant
2. directly over the flame. Using a pair of tongs, turn the eggplant every 5 minutes or so until it
3. is tender and the skin is charred and crispy on all sides (20 minutes.) The eggplant should
4. deflate and become super tender. supposed to. If you don't have a gas burner you can use a

**grill. You can also roast the eggplant in the oven (see notes).**
5. Baba Ganoush Recipe - The Mediterranean Dish
2. Remove the eggplant from the heat and transfer it to a large colander over a bowl. Allow it to
3. sit and drain for a few minutes until fully cooled and all excess water has been drained (it
4. helps if you open the eggplant up a bit and push on it with a knife or a spoon to help it
5. release its juices).
3. Once the eggplant is cool enough to touch, peel the charred crispy skin off (it should come
4. right off). Discard the skin and the stem (don't worry if a few bits of the skin remain, that is
5. just added flavor).
4. Transfer the cooked and fully drained eggplant to a bowl. Use a fork to break it down into
5. smaller pieces. Add the tahini paste, garlic, lemon juice, Greek yogurt (if using) salt, pepper,
6. sumac, Aleppo pepper or crushed red pepper flakes. Mix gently with a wooden spoon or a
7. fork until well-combined.
5. Cover the baba ganoush and chill in the fridge for 30 minutes to an hour.
6. To serve, transfer the baba ganoush to a rimmed serving dish or a bowl. Top with a good
7. drizzle of extra virgin olive oil and toasted pine nuts, if you like. Serve with pita wedges or pita
8. chips and veggies of your choice!

## Notes
To roast the eggplant in the oven instead: heat the oven to 425 degrees F. Trim the
eggplant and cut them in half, then salt it and allow it to "sweat out" excess water for about
30 minutes or so. Wipe it off, and arrange the eggplant on a lightly-oiled baking sheet, flesh
side down. Roast for about 40 minutes or until very tender and cooked through. Allow the
eggplant time to cool a bit, then using a spoon, scoop up the flesh and place it in a bowl.
Follow the recipe from step #4.
For best texture, mix the eggplant as directed using a wooden spoon or a fork rather
than a food processor. This dip is meant to be creamy but on the rustic side with some
texture.
Store leftovers in a tightly-closed container in the fridge for up to 4 days.

and spices.

# Béarnaise Sauce Recipe

Béarnaise sauce is a piquant child of hollandaise, one of the so-called mother sauces of French cuisine. It is simply an emulsification — egg

## Overview
- **Total Time**: 20 minutes
- **Servings**: 4 servings Step 1

## Recipe

Béarnaise Sauce
By Sam Sifton
Total Time 20 minutes
Rating (1,003)
Béarnaise sauce is a piquant child of hollandaise, one of the so-called mother sauces of French cuisine. It is simply an emulsification — egg
yolks and butter cut through with vinegar flavored with tarragon and shallots, with a bite of black pepper. Think of it as a loose mayonnaise,
requiring only plenty of whisking and a careful hand with the heat to master. You donʼt need the clarified butter many recipes call for — a
good unsalted butter, melted, works just fine. Apply the sauce to steaks or burgers, asparagus or salmon. The sauceʼs richness improves
virtually everything it touches.
INGREDIENTS PREPARATION
Yield: 4 servings Step 1
Put the vinegar, shallots, black pepper and 1 tablespoon of tarragon leaves into a small
saucepan, and set over a medium flame. Bring just to a boil, and then reduce heat to a
¼ cup white-wine vinegar
simmer until there are only a few tablespoons of liquid left, approximately 5 minutes.
1 small shallot, peeled and minced
Remove from heat, and set aside to cool.
½ teaspoon freshly cracked black pepper
1 tablespoon plus 1 teaspoon chopped tarragon
Step 2
leaves
Fill a small saucepan with an inch or two of water, and set over medium-high heat to boil.
2 egg yolks
12 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted
Step 3
Kosher salt, to taste
Put the cooled shallot-and-tarragon mixture into a metal mixing bowl along with a
Splash of lemon juice, optional
tablespoon of water and the egg yolks, then whisk to combine.
Step 4
Turn the heat under the saucepan of water down to its lowest setting, and put the bowl on
top of the pan, making sure that it does not touch the water directly. Continue to whisk the
yolks until they thicken, approximately 5 to 7 minutes. You should just about double the
volume of the yolks.
Step 5
Slowly beat in the butter, a tablespoon or two at a time, whisking slowly to combine and
emulsify. Remove the bowl from the pan occasionally, so as not to overcook the eggs, and
taste the sauce. Season with salt. If the flavor is not sharp enough, add a splash of lemon
juice. If the sauce is too thick, stir in a splash of hot water. Add the remaining teaspoon of
tarragon leaves, and serve.

content:
# Beef Bourguignon

Beef Bourguignon - Cafe Delites

## Overview
- **Total Time**: 15 mins 3 hrs 3 hrs 15 mins
- **Servings**: 6 - 8 people

## Ingredients
- 1 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
- 6 ounces bacon roughly chopped
- 3 pounds beef brisket trimmed of fat, chuck steak or stewing beef cut into 2-inch chunks
- 1 carrot large, sliced ½-inch thick
- 1 white onion large, diced
- 6 cloves garlic minced (divided)
- 1 pinch coarse salt
- 1 pinch ground pepper
- 2 tablespoons flour
- 12 pearl onions small, optional
- 3 cups red wine like Merlot, Pinot Noir, or a Chianti - for a milder sauce, use only 2 cups of wine
- 2-3 cups beef stock (if using 2 cups of wine, use 3 cups beef stock)
- 2 tablespoons tomato paste
- 1 beef bouillon cube crushed
- 1 teaspoon fresh thyme finely chopped
- 2 tablespoons fresh parsley finely chopped, divided
- 2 bay leaves
- 1 pound white mushrooms fresh, small or brown mushrooms ,quartered
- 2 tablespoons butter

## Instructions
1. Beef Bourguignon - Cafe Delites

**TRADITIONAL OVEN METHOD:**
1. Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
2. Heat the oil in a large dutch oven or heavy based pot. Sauté the bacon over medium heat for about 3
3. minutes, until crisp and browned. Transfer with a slotted spoon to a large dish and set aside.
3. Pat dry beef with paper towel; sear in batches in the hot oil/bacon fat until browned on all sides. Remove to
4. the dish with the bacon.
4. In the remaining oil/bacon fat, sauté the carrots and diced onions until softened, (about 3 minutes), then add
5. 4 cloves minced garlic and cook for 1 minute. Drain excess fat (leave about 1 tablespoon in the pan) and
6. return the bacon and beef back into the pot; season with ½ teaspoon coarse salt and ¼ teaspoon ground
7. pepper. Sprinkle with flour, toss well and cook for 4-5 minutes to brown.
5. Add the pearl onions, wine and enough stock so that the meat is barely covered. Then add the tomato paste,
6. bullion and herbs. Bring to a simmer on the stove.
6. Cover, transfer to lower part of the oven and simmer for 2 to 3 hours, or until the meat is fall apart tender
7. (adjust the heat so that the liquid simmers very slowly).
7. In the last 5 minutes of cooking time, prepare your mushrooms:
8. Heat the butter in a medium-sized skillet/pan over heat. When the foam subsides, add the remaining 2 cloves
9. garlic and cook until fragrant (about 30 seconds), then add in the mushrooms. Cook for about 5 minutes,
10. while shaking the pan occasionally to coat with the butter. Season with salt and pepper, if desired. Once they
11. are browned, set aside.

# Beef Burritos

Recipe video above. Simple, super tasty everyday beef burritos made with a

## Overview
- **Total Time**: 15 mins 20 mins 35 mins
- **Servings**: 6 - 8 burritos

## Ingredients
- Burrito Seasoning:
- 1 tsp each onion powder , dried oregano, salt
- 2 tsp each dried cumin powder , paprika
- 1/4 tsp black pepper
- ¼ tsp cayenne pepper , or to taste (optional)
- Beef:
- 1/2 tbsp olive oil
- 2 garlic cloves
- ½ onion , finely chopped
- 500g / 1 lb beef mince (ground beef), I use lean
- 2 tbsp tomato paste
- 3 tbsp water
- Burritos:
- 6 - 8 large soft flour tortillas or round wraps (~25cm/10”+) (Note 1)
- 3 cups cooked rice , warm not piping hot (I use white long grain)
- 3 cups iceberg lettuce or cabbage , finely sliced (use cabbage if freezing)
- 1 cup corn kernels (I use canned, drained)
- 1 cup black beans (I use canned, drained)
- 3 tomatoes, deseeded and diced
- 1/2 red onion , finely chopped
- Finely chopped coriander / cilantro (optional)
- 1 1/2 cups / 150g shredded cheese of choice (melting kind)

## Instructions
1. Heat oil in a skillet over high heat. Add garlic and onion, cook for 2 minutes until onion is
2. lightly browned. Add beef and cook, breaking it up as you go, until it turns from red to
3. brown.
4. Beef Burritos - RecipeTin Eats
2. Add Taco Seasoning (or use 1 packet store bought) and cook for 1 minute. Then add tomato
3. paste and water, cook for 3 minutes until the water is mostly evaporated but the beef is still
4. juicy, not dried out. Set aside to cool for 10 minutes – piping hot filling will steam the burrito,
5. making the tortilla soggy.
3. Optional: If not warming rolled burrito, warm the tortillas before rolling (per packet
4. directions).
4. Place a burrito on a work surface. Place 1/4 - 1/3 cup of rice just below the centre. Top with
5. 1/4 - 1/3 cup beef, then some lettuce, corn, black beans, tomato, a sprinkle of red onion,
6. coriander and cheese.
5. Fold up the bottom to cover the filling then fold the edges in (video helpful to see how to do
6. this). Roll up tightly, then wrap in foil. Serve as is or heat per below.
6. HEATING: To warm through, pan fry (dry pan) in the foil over medium high heat for a few
7. minutes on each side to slightly crisp and warm the outside. Or for 10+ minutes on a medium
8. low heat if you want to melt the cheese. Or they can be baked at 180C/350F for 20 minutes in
9. the foil – this will warm them all the way through and crisp up the tortilla slightly. If they are
10. straight from the fridge, they will take around 30 minutes to warm through.
7. Burritos are best served with something to dollop/dip - sour cream (or yoghurt) and some
8. sort of chilli sauce are my usual because it's easy. When I'm making more of an effort, I use
9. Restaurant Style Salsa or Guacamole.

## Notes
1. I like to use Mission large soft wraps (see photo in post) because they are slightly larger than
burrito wraps sold in the Mexican section of Woolies/Coles etc plus they are slightly softer so less
prone to breaking AND they are slightly cheaper. Win, win, win! (PS I'm in Australia :) )
2. STORAGE/REHEATING: Burritos freeze / reheat brilliantly as long as you avoid watery vegetables.
The combination of ingredients I use (don't use lettuce, use green cabbage) is ideal for freezing.
Typically, tomatoes aren't great for freezing but because it's the only "watery" vegetable and not
much is used, it works great. To reheat, thaw for 24 hours in the fridge or overnight on counter (as
log as it's not super hot where you are) then:
- OVEN: reheat in oven at 180C/350F in foil for 30 - 4o min (place on tray in case there is leakage)
until outside is slightly crisp;- MICROWAVE/STOVE: unwrap then microwave for 2 minutes then
crisp in dry pan over medium heat;- STOVE: Leave in foil and turn over medium heat in dry pan for
10+ minutes until crisp all over (takes a while to warm all the way through).
3. MORE VEGGIES / Great for Freezing: One way to pack more veggies into this and/or reduce the
carbs by leaving out the rice is to add veggies into the beef filling. To do this, increase the
Seasoning, tomato and water by 50% (use the scaler by hovering your cursor over Servings) then
add 3 cups of diced veggies of choice, like zucchini, carrots, celery, capsicum, corn. Use a large
skillet, saute these veggies after the onion, then push to the side and add the beef and proceed
with the recipe.

## Recipe

Beef Stroganoff
By Craig Claiborne
Updated Feb. 28, 2024
Total Time 45 minutes
Rating (2,472)
This classic recipe appeared in a 1963 Times article by Craig Claiborne about the increasing popularity of beef stroganoff (the article
featured not one, but two slightly different recipes for the dish.) Mr. Claiborne reported that “the meat-and-cream dish is of Russian
provenance, likely named for a noted Russian gourmet, Count Paul Stroganoff, a dignitary in the court of Czar Alexander III.” Stroganoff
may not be considered haute cuisine any longer, but the rich stew, dotted with mushrooms and laced with sour cream, is still deeply
satisfying and the perfect antidote to a chilly day. Serve it over buttered parsley noodles.
INGREDIENTS PREPARATION
Yield: 4 to 6 servings Step 1
Combine the flour, salt and pepper. Dredge the meat in the mixture.

title: Beef Tenderloin
description: A simple yet elegant preparation for a 5lb whole filet mignon, featuring a rosemary-garlic compound butter.
content:
A simple yet elegant preparation for a 5lb whole filet mignon, featuring a rosemary-garlic compound butter.

## Compound Butter
- 1 cup unsalted butter, softened
- 3 tbsp fresh rosemary, chopped
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tsp black pepper
- 1 tsp sea salt

## Filet
- 5 lb whole filet mignon
- 2 tbsp kosher salt
- 2 tbsp black pepper

## Instructions
1. Make compound butter: Mix ingredients, roll in plastic wrap, refrigerate until firm
2. Bring filet to room temp (1 hour), pat dry, season with salt and pepper
3. Preheat to 450°F
4. Place on roasting rack, top with half the butter
5. Sear 15 min at 450°F
6. Reduce to 350°F, cook to temp:
   - Rare: 120-125°F (~20-25 min)
   - Medium-Rare: 130-135°F (~25-30 min)
   - Medium: 140-145°F (~30-35 min)
7. Remove 5°F below target temp
8. Add remaining butter, tent with foil
9. Rest 15-20 minutes before slicing

## Notes
- Use meat thermometer in thickest part
- Temperature rises ~5°F while resting
- Slice against grain, 1-1.5 inch portions

# Best-Ever Key Lime Pie

## Overview

## Ingredients
**FOR THE CRUST**
- 1½ cups �nely crushed graham cracker crumbs, from about 12 whole
- graham crackers
- ⅓ cup packed light brown sugar
- 4 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted

**FOR THE FILLING**
- Two 14-oz cans sweetened condensed milk
- 1 cup plain Greek yogurt (2% or whole milk)
- 1 tablespoon grated lime zest
- ¾ cup fresh lime juice

**FOR THE TOPPING**
- 1 cup cold heavy cream
- 2 tablespoons confectioners' sugar
- 1 teaspoon grated lime zest
- 8 to 10 thin lime slices

## Instructions
1. FOR THE CRUST
2. Preheat oven to 375 °F and set an oven rack in the middle position.
3. In a medium bowl, combine the graham cracker crumbs, brown sugar, and melted butter; stir with a fork �rst, and then your hands
4. until the mixture is well combined. Using your �ngers and the bottom of a glass or dry measuring cup, press the crumbs �rmly into
5. the bottom and up the sides of a 9 x 1.5-inch (deep-dish) pie pan. e crust should be about ¼-inch thick. (Tip: do the sides �rst.)
6. Bake for 10 minutes, until just slightly browned. Let the crust cool on a wire rack.
7. Best-Ever Key Lime Pie - Once Upon a Chef
8. FOR THE FILLING
9. Lower the oven temperature to 350°F.
10. In a large bowl, whisk together the sweetened condensed milk, yogurt, lime zest, and lime juice. Pour the thick mixture into the
11. warm graham cracker crust. Bake for 15 minutes, until the �lling is almost set; it should wobble a bit. Let cool at room temperature
12. for 30 minutes, then place in the refrigerator to chill thoroughly, about 3 hours.
13. FOR THE TOPPING
14. In the bowl of an electric mixer, beat the heavy cream until so peaks form. Add the confectioners’ sugar and beat until medium
15. peaks form. Top the pie with the whipped cream. Decorate with the lime zest and lime slices. Store the pie in the refrigerator until
16. ready to serve. Slice the pie into wedges, wiping your knife clean between slices, and serve cold.
17. Make-Ahead Instructions: You can make the crust a day ahead of time, but the �lling should be added on the day of serving,
18. otherwise the crust will get soggy.

## Instructions
1. For the broth:
1. Heat the oil in a tall pot (I use an 8 quart stockpot) over medium heat. Add the onion and leek and cook gently until softened.
2. Stir in the garlic and cook for a minute until fragrant, then add the tomatoes, water, herbs, orange peel, saffron, salt and fish
3. bones and shrimp shells. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat so that the broth bubbles slowly without boiling.
2. Cook 30 minutes, then strain the broth into a large bowl or another pot and discard the solids.
3. Pour the broth back into the stockpot and bring to a boil. Add the shrimp and cook until they turn pink, a minute or two. Add
4. the rest of the fish and shellfish, cover and simmer until the mussels or clams open (this will just take a few minutes).
4. Taste the soup and add more salt and freshly ground pepper if needed.
5. Make the rouille:
1. Puree everything except for the olive oil in a food processor until smooth. Slowly add the olive oil while processing to form a
2. paste.

2. Toast the bread and brush with olive oil.
3. Serve the soup with bread and rouille.

## Notes
For a heartier soup, serve over cooked broken vermicelli, orzo or other small pasta shape.
The broth can be prepared up to a day in advance. Store in the refrigerator and bring to a simmer. Add the seafood and cook
as in Step 3.

title: Broccoli Rabe & Leek Salmon with Basil Broth
description: A clean, herbaceous dish featuring broiled salmon over chunky broccoli rabe and leek in a light basil-infused chicken broth. The salmon is marinated to integrate with the vegetables, creating a cohesive plate with bright lemon finishing.
content:
# Broccoli Rabe & Leek Salmon with Basil Broth

A clean, herbaceous dish featuring broiled salmon over chunky broccoli rabe and leek in a light basil-infused chicken broth. The salmon is marinated to integrate with the vegetables, creating a cohesive plate with bright lemon finishing.

---

## Recipe Details

- **Prep Time:** 40 minutes (includes marinating)
- **Cook Time:** 25 minutes
- **Total Time:** 65 minutes
- **Servings:** 4
- **Dietary Notes:** Dairy-free, gluten-free (if using gluten-free broth)

---

## Ingredients

### Herb & Lemon Marinade (for Salmon)

- 3 tablespoons olive oil
- Zest and juice of 1 lemon
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 tablespoon fresh basil, torn
- Salt and pepper to taste
- 4 salmon fillets (6 ounces each, skin on, about 1 to 1¼ inches thick)

### Broccoli Rabe & Leek Base

- 1½ pounds broccoli rabe, roughly chopped
- 3 medium leeks (white and light green parts only), halved lengthwise and sliced into half-moons
- 4 tablespoons olive oil, divided
- Salt and pepper to taste
- ¾ to 1 cup chicken broth
- ¾ cup fresh basil, loosely packed
- 2-3 tablespoons olive oil, for finishing

### Finishing

- 1 lemon, cut into wedges
- Fleur de sel (or sea salt)
- Freshly ground black pepper

---

## Instructions

### Prepare the Marinade (15 minutes before cooking)

1. In a small bowl, combine 3 tablespoons olive oil, lemon zest, lemon juice, minced garlic, torn basil, salt, and pepper.

2. Place salmon fillets skin-side down on a plate or shallow dish. Pour marinade over the fillets, making sure they're evenly coated.

3. Let sit at room temperature for 30-60 minutes while you prepare the vegetables.

### Make the Broccoli Rabe & Leek Base

1. Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.

2. Add sliced leeks with a pinch of salt. Cook gently for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened and jammy. The leeks should begin to caramelize at the edges but not brown aggressively.

3. Add chopped broccoli rabe with the remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil and another pinch of salt.

4. Cook over medium-high heat for 5-7 minutes, stirring frequently, until the rabe is completely tender. You want some color and browning at the edges—this adds depth.

5. Pour in the chicken broth and simmer for 2-3 minutes to marry the flavors. Taste and adjust salt as needed.

6. Remove the skillet from heat.

7. Fold in the fresh basil and 2-3 tablespoons finishing olive oil. Do not blend. The vegetables should remain chunky and textured, with the broth binding them loosely.

8. If the mixture seems too thick, add a splash more broth (a few tablespoons at a time). If too thin, let it simmer uncovered for another minute or two.

9. Keep warm over low heat, or set aside and gently reheat before serving.

### Broil the Salmon

1. Preheat your oven to 400°F with the rack positioned in the upper-middle area (about 6 inches from the broiler element).

2. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

3. Remove salmon fillets from marinade and place skin-side down on the prepared baking sheet.

4. Bake at 400°F for 8-10 minutes until the salmon is just barely cooked through. The flesh should be opaque but still slightly translucent at the thickest part.

5. Switch the oven to broil (high setting) and broil for 1-2 minutes until the top is lightly caramelized and the flesh is fully opaque. Watch carefully—this step happens quickly.

6. Remove from the oven immediately.

### Plate and Finish

1. Spoon the broccoli rabe and leek broth into shallow bowls or onto individual plates, distributing the chunky vegetables evenly.

2. Set one broiled salmon fillet on top of the broth, skin-side down.

3. Finish with a squeeze of fresh lemon juice, a small pinch of fleur de sel, and a few grinds of freshly ground black pepper.

4. Serve immediately with lemon wedges on the side.

---

## Notes

**On the marinade:** The garlic, lemon, and basil in the salmon marinade will mingle with the broth as you eat, creating a unified, herbaceous flavor profile. Don't skip this step.

**On texture:** The vegetables are intentionally chunky. Resist the urge to blend or puree. The bitter rabe, jammy leeks, and leafy basil should all be visible and textured in the broth.

**On the broth consistency:** The goal is a light, brothy sauce that coats a spoon, not a thick puree or a thin soup. Start with ¾ cup broth and add more if needed. You can always add broth, but you can't remove it.

**On salmon doneness:** The two-temperature approach (low oven, then broil) ensures even, gentle cooking with a caramelized top. Don't skip the initial bake or rely on broil alone—you'll end up with an overcooked exterior and raw center.

**On timing:** The base can be made 1-2 hours ahead and gently reheated. The salmon should be cooked fresh just before serving for best texture.

**On basil:** Tear the basil by hand rather than chopping to minimize oxidation and browning.

**Optional garnish:** A small fresh basil leaf placed on top of the salmon adds a subtle finishing touch.

---

## Variations & Substitutions

- **For a lighter broth:** Use vegetable broth instead of chicken broth.
- **For more assertive flavor:** Add ½ teaspoon Dijon mustard or a splash of white wine to the broth during simmering.
- **For added texture:** Scatter a few halved cherry tomatoes around the plate for brightness (optional).
- **Alternative greens:** Lacinato kale or Swiss chard can be substituted for broccoli rabe, though they lack the characteristic bitterness.

---

## Serving Suggestions

Serve with a crisp white wine (Vermentino, Albariño, or dry Riesling) that echoes the herbaceous, lemony notes of the dish. A simple green salad with lemon vinaigrette complements the meal without weighing it down.

---

## Storage

Leftover broth and vegetables can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Reheat gently over low heat, adding a splash of broth if needed. Do not reheat the salmon; it's best fresh.

content:
# Butternut Squash Congee with Chile Oil

## Description
This recipe offers a seasonal twist on traditional congee, incorporating butternut squash for a warming, naturally sweet, and earthy flavor. The addition of chile oil provides a lively contrast to the mellow nature of the dish, delivering both heat and savoriness.

## Ingredients
- 2 cups leftover medium- or long-grain rice (preferably refrigerated)
- 1 tablespoon neutral oil
- 1 teaspoon kosher salt
- 6 cups vegetable stock
- 4 garlic cloves, peeled and crushed
- 1 pound butternut squash, peeled, seeded, and diced into 1-inch pieces
- 1 small piece kombu (optional)
- 2 scallions, finely sliced
- Chile oil or chile crisp, for serving

## Instructions
1. Combine rice, oil, and salt in a large pot, breaking up any clumps.
2. Add stock, garlic, squash, and kombu (if using). Bring to a boil over medium-high heat.
3. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes.
4. Uncover, stir, and simmer for another 5-10 minutes on medium heat until rice breaks down.
5. Remove from heat and discard larger seaweed pieces if used.
6. Stir vigorously to break up rice, squash, and garlic.
7. Season with salt to taste.
8. Serve topped with scallions and chile oil or crisp.

## Notes
- Using leftover rice yields a hearty congee in about 30 minutes.
- For easier handling, cut butternut squash into smaller pieces before peeling.
- Pre-cut butternut squash cubes can be used for convenience.
- The dish is not traditional to any specific region but is a seasonal interpretation of congee.

## Yield
4 to 6 servings

## Time
Total time: 45 minutes

At this point, you may need to adjust the texture of the fondue to make it just right for

4. Add the chicken broth in small splashes, stirring continuously. Scrape up any remnants from
5. the bottom of the pot as you do so. Add the half and half in the same manner. Add the
6. chicken bouillon, if using.
5. Add frozen peas. Bring to a gentle boil and let it simmer, uncovered, while you make the
6. dumplings.
7. Make the Dumplings
1. Combine the flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, garlic powder, and sugar in a
2. medium bowl.
2. Add the milk, sour cream, and melted butter. Use a folding motion to combine and form a
3. dough, but don’t overmix or they will be dense.
3. Add the chicken back to the soup along with any juices from the plate. Stir to combine and
4. reduce heat to low. (If using leftover chicken, add it now.)
4. Use a small cookie scoop and carefully place the dumplings over the soup in an even layer.
5. Spoon a little liquid over each one.
5. Cover tightly and increase heat slightly to bring it to a gentle simmer. Set a timer for 15
6. minutes, don’t lift the lid during this time, the dumplings need to steam.
6. Open the lid and insert a toothpick into the middle of a dumpling to check for doneness. If it
7. comes out clean, it’s ready. If not, cover and simmer for a few more minutes.
7. Once the middle is set, garnish with parsley and serve!

Just as beautiful for entertaining as it is for a comforting family meal, biryani is a Central and South Asian dish of layered rice, spices and

# Chicken Stew

This Chicken Stew has juicy chicken in a savory broth with a perfect blend

## Overview
- **Total Time**: 15 mins 1 hr 30 mins 1 hr 45 mins
- **Servings**: 6 people Calories

## Ingredients
- Chicken
- 1-2 tablespoons olive oil
- Salt/Pepper
- 2 teaspoons Italian seasoning
- 2 lbs. bone-in chicken breast or thighs see notes
- Stew
- ½ cup dry white wine see notes
- 5 tablespoons butter
- 1 medium yellow onion diced
- 1 ½ cups carrots diced
- 2 ribs celery diced
- 4 cloves garlic minced
- 1 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce
- 1 teaspoon hot sauce
- 1/3 cup flour
- 6 cups Chicken Broth
- ½ cup heavy cream optional
- 1 chicken bouillon cube or 1 tsp. better than bouillon
- 1.5 lbs. red potatoes washed/dried
- 2-3 drops Gravy Master optional, see link in notes.
- Seasonings
- 1 teaspoon dried parsley
- ½ teaspoon EACH: dried basil, rosemary, thyme, mustard powder, onion powder
- ¼ teaspoon EACH: ground sage, salt, celery salt
- 1/8 teaspoon pepper

## Instructions
1. Prep Work: Measure out ingredients before beginning, it makes the process easier and more
2. relaxing. (Don't cut the potatoes yet.)
2. Pat the chicken dry and season each side with salt, pepper, and Italian seasoning.
3. Chicken Stew - The Cozy Cook
3. Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or soup pot over medium-high heat. Make sure the pot
4. is sufficiently heated so that the chicken sears right when it hits it. Add the chicken and cook
5. for 3-4 minutes/side, then remove and set aside. (We want the middle to be uncooked.) Don’t
6. cut up the chicken yet.
4. Turn off the heat. Add the wine and set the heat to medium. Use a silicone spatula to “clean”
5. the bottom and sides of the pot. Let the liquid reduce by half, about 4 minutes.
5. Add the butter and let it melt. Add the onions, carrots, and celery. Toss to coat. Soften for
6. 5 minutes.
6. Add the garlic, hot sauce, Worcestershire sauce, and seasonings. Cook for 1 minute.
7. Add the flour and stir to combine. Cook for 2 minutes, or until it begins to turn a golden
8. brown.
8. Add the chicken broth in small splashes, stirring continuously. Be sure to do this slowly. Add
9. the heavy cream in the same manner. Next, add the chicken bouillon.
9. Bring the stew to a boil, then reduce to a gentle simmer. Add the whole pieces of chicken
10. back along with any juices from the plate.
10. Cover partially and let it bubble very gently, partially covered, for 45-60 minutes. It will
11. reduce, thicken, and concentrate. Don’t let it reach a boil or the chicken will be tough/dry. (A
12. few gentle bubbles are good.) Stir occasionally as it cooks.
11. Use kitchen tongs to remove the chicken and set aside on a plate. Let it rest. Cut the
12. potatoes into 3/4-inch chunks and add them to the stew Simmer until fork tender, about
13. 20 minutes.
12. Dice or shred the chicken and discard any bones. Return it to the stew. Optional: Add
13. a few drops of gravy master to add a slightly darker color to this stew. Taste and add any
14. additional seasoning if desired. Serve with cheddar bay biscuits or buttermilk biscuits!

## Notes
Pro Tips:
A few drops of Gravy Master or Kitchen Bouquet can add a slightly darker color to this stew
if preferred, but it's not necessary!
Flavor Enhancers: The Worcestershire sauce, hot sauce, and mustard powder in this recipe
are used as flavor enhancers and can't be tasted outright. I use Frank's Hot Sauce.
Wine: Pinot Grigio, Chardonnay, or Sauvignon Blanc are great in this recipe. Chicken
broth can be used if you don’t cook with wine.
Frozen peas, corn, or green beans can be stirred in 10-15 minutes prior to serving if desired.
For even more flavor, add the rind from a block of Parmesan or Romano cheese when you
simmer the stew. If any remains at the end of cooking, it can be discarded.
My Ranch Oyster Crackers make a great topping for soups and stews, or pair this with my
crusty, airy, No Knead Bread for dipping!
Be sure to try my Chicken and Dumplings recipe next!

# Chicken Tortilla Soup

## Description
This recipe for Chicken Tortilla Soup is adapted from a dish served at the Rose Garden restaurant in Anthony, Texas. It uses chicken legs as the base of the stock and adds beef bones for extra depth. The soup is known for its rich flavor and hearty texture.

## Ingredients
- 2½ pounds bone-in chicken thighs or legs
- 1 pound beef bones (optional)
- 1 medium onion, quartered (skin on)
- 1 head garlic, halved across the equator (skin on)
- ¼ cup vegetable oil, or more as needed
- 6 corn tortillas
- Salt
- 2 tablespoons canned chipotle chilies in adobo, or to taste
- ½ cup chopped fresh cilantro
- 2 avocados, pitted, peeled and cubed
- 4 to 8 ounces plain melting cheese (like mozzarella, Oaxaca or Jack), shredded or cubed
- Lime wedges for serving (optional)

## Instructions
1. In a large pot, combine chicken, beef bones (if using), 3 onion quarters, and garlic. Cover with water (about 10 cups) and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer for 45 minutes to 1 hour, skimming foam occasionally.

2. Meanwhile, fry 2 tortillas in vegetable oil until crisp. Drain and set aside. Cut remaining tortillas into strips and fry until crisp. Drain and salt while warm.

3. Remove chicken from pot when tender. Cool and shred the meat, discarding bones and skin.

4. Strain the stock and discard solids. 

5. Blend the remaining onion quarter, chipotle, ¼ cup cilantro, salt, and the two whole fried tortillas with some stock until smooth.

6. Return purée and remaining stock to the pot. Boil, then simmer for 5-10 minutes.

7. Add shredded chicken and adjust salt if needed.

8. Serve soup in bowls, garnished with avocados, cheese, remaining cilantro, and fried tortilla strips. Offer lime wedges on the side.

## Yield
4 to 6 servings

## Time
Total time: 1½ hours

## Notes
- The recipe is adaptable and can be tweaked to personal taste.
- For a richer flavor, consider browning the chicken and adding vegetables like carrots and celery to the stock.
- Some cooks add black beans, diced tomatoes, or corn for extra substance.
- Epazote leaves, found in Mexican stores, can add an authentic flavor to the soup.

# Chile Con Queso

This Chile Con Queso recipe is delicious, spicy, silky, super cheesy and

## Overview
- **Total Time**: 10 mins 15 mins 25 mins
- **Servings**: 8 Calories

## Ingredients
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- ½ pound ground beef extra lean
- 1 teaspoon chili powder
- 1 small red onion diced
- 1 clove garlic minced
- 4 ounce green chiles (1 can)
- 1 jalapeno fresh, seeded and chopped
- 14 ounce fire roasted tomatoes (1 can)
- 1 cup evaporated milk
- 1 cup velveeta cubed
- 2½ cups monterery jack cheese shredded
- 1 tablespoon cilantro fresh, chopped

## Instructions
1. Heat the olive oil in a cast iron skillet, or oven safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add the
2. ground beef to the skillet, season it with the chili powder, and cook for about 5 minutes until
3. no longer pink, breaking it up as you go along.
2. Stir in the red onion and garlic and cook for 2 more minutes or until the onion softens and
3. becomes translucent.
3. Add the green chiles, jalapeno, fire roasted tomatoes and stir. Bring to a simmer, then turn
4. down the heat to medium low. Add the evaporated milk and velveeta and cook for 2 more
5. minutes or until the velveeta melts. Stir in 2 cups of the jack cheese and cook for another
6. minute until it melts.
4. Turn off the heat. Sprinkle the remaining jack cheese over the top of the dip and place the
5. skillet over the broiler for about 5 minutes or until browned and bubbly. Watch it so it doesn't
6. burn.
5. Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve with tortilla chips.

## Notes
1/2
 Chile Con Queso - Jo Cooks
1. Meatless option: Skip the beef, just saute the onion, garlic in the olive oil and then continue
with the rest of the steps.
2. What is evaporated milk: Evaporated milk, also known as unsweetened condensed milk in
some countries, is a canned milk product with about 60% of the water removed from fresh
milk. It's a dense, creamy, and ultra-concentrated milk. You can usually find it in the baking
aisle at your local grocery store.
3. Why use evaporated milk: It's used in this dip to provide extra creaminess or body without
the fat of real cream.
4. Why velveeta: I used velveeta because if you truly want a silky queso, velveeta is the way to
go, however feel free to use any shredded cheese you prefer such as Monterey Jack, Cheddar,
etc, anything that is a great melting cheese.
5. I don't have fire roasted tomatoes, can I use something else: Yes, of course. You can use
regular canned diced tomatoes or just fresh tomatoes and chop them up yourself. I like the
smoky flavor from the fire roasted tomatoes, which is why I chose it for this recipe.
6. I don't have a cast iron skillet, can I use something else: Yes! Feel free to use any skillet
that is oven safe. If you don't have an oven safe skillet, transfer the chile con queso to a 9x13
baking dish or a 9 inch round baking dish.
7. I can't find canned green chiles, what else can I use: Keep in mind that canned green chiles
are not really spicy at all, so one substitute could be roasted bell peppers.
8. Is this dip spicy: Yes, it is. It's spicy because I use a whole jalapeno pepper, and my jalapeno
was quite big, so feel free to omit it or use as much or as little as you like.
9. What can I serve this dip with: I love to serve this with tortilla chips, carrots and celery
sticks. However, any crispy crackers would also work.

# Chinese Eggplant in Garlic Sauce

This recipe focuses on achieving crispy Chinese eggplant coated in a rich garlic sauce. The eggplant is first soaked in saltwater to draw out moisture, then stir-fried until soft and golden. The garlic sauce, made with soy sauce, sugar, and a touch of dark soy for color, is quickly tossed with the eggplant to ensure it stays crispy and flavorful. The dish can be served as a side or as a main dish over rice.

- **Preparation Time**: 25 minutes
- **Cook Time**: 15 minutes
- **Total Time**: 40 minutes
- **Servings**: 2-4

## Ingredients:
- 2 Chinese eggplants
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 1 tablespoon cornstarch
- 2 tablespoons sesame oil
- 1 teaspoon ginger, minced
- 3 cloves garlic, chopped

### Sauce:
- 1 tablespoon light soy sauce
- 1 tablespoon water
- 1/2 teaspoon dark soy sauce
- 2 teaspoons sugar
- 1 teaspoon cornstarch

## Instructions:
1. **Prep the Eggplant**: Soak eggplant in saltwater, then pat dry.
2. **Fry the Eggplant**: Stir-fry the eggplant until soft and golden.
3. **Prepare the Sauce**: Mix the sauce ingredients.
4. **Finish the Dish**: Add the sauce to the cooked eggplant and stir until well coated.

For full instructions, visit [Omnivore's Cookbook](https://omnivorescookbook.com/chinese-eggplant-garlic-sauce).

# Chopped Steak Recipe

Chopped Steak Recipe - Chef Billy Parisi

## Overview
- **Prep Time**: 20 minutes
- **Cook Time**: 30 minutes
- **Total Time**: 50 minutes
- **Servings**: 4

## Ingredients
- 6 strips diced smoked uncured bacon
- 2 pounds ground sirloin, formed into 8 ounce patties
- 2 small peeled thickly sliced yellow onions
- 4 cups domestic mushrooms, cut in half
- 4 cups beef stock
- 2 teaspoons fresh thyme
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 4 shredded Idaho potatoes
- coarse salt and cracked fresh pepper to taste
- 1/4
- Chopped Steak Recipe - Chef Billy Parisi

## Instructions
1. 1 Season the beef patties with salt and pepper and set aside.
2. 2 In a hot large saute pan over medium heat add in bacon and cook until crispy. Once the bacon is cooked reserve
3. to the side and use the same pan to add seasoned meat.
4. 3 Sear the meat for 2 to 3 minutes per side until browned but not cooked through.
5. 4 Remove the chopped steaks from the pan once brown and set aside on a plate. Next, add the onions and
6. mushrooms to the pan, turn the heat down to medium, and caramelize for about 12 to 15 minutes.
7. 5 Once the vegetables are nice and golden brown, deglaze with the beef stock add in the thyme, salt, and pepper,
8. and bring to a boil.
9. 6 Add the bacon and chopped steaks and simmer over low heat for 20 to 25 minutes or until the vegetables are
10. tender and the chopped steak is cooked through.
11. 7 As an optional side, In a separate large saute pan over medium-high heat add in the olive oil and shredded
12. potatoes. Cook for 20 to 25 minutes, flipping the potatoes over every 4 to 5 minutes until golden brown. Season
13. with salt and pepper.
14. 8 Serve the chopped steak with the onions, mushrooms, gravy, and optional hash browns side dish.

## Notes
Make-Ahead: These are meant to be eaten when they're done cooking. However, you can keep them warm in a pan
with the mushroom and onion gravy, covered, for up to 1 hour over very low heat.
 2/4
 Chopped Steak Recipe - Chef Billy Parisi
How to Store: Store this chopped steak in a plastic container or cover it in plastic and refrigerate for up to 4 days. It
can also be frozen for up to 3 months and covered in plastic. Thaw for 1 day in the refrigerator before reheating.
How to Reheat: Add your desired portions to a sauté pan with a 1/4 cup of beef stock, cover in foil, and cook in the
oven at 400° for 10 to 12 minutes. Reheating your steak will 100% cause it to increase in internal temperature, most
likely past medium and into medium-well.
The #/# ratios you see for beef represent lean meat-to-fat. The first number is always lean, and the second is always
fat.
If you do not want to use bacon in this recipe, substitute the bacon fat with 2 tablespoons of olive or avocado oil, lard,
ghee, clarified butter, or beef tallow.
True caramelized onions take about 45 minutes or so to caramelize properly.
When cooking the onions, you can add a bit of water or wine to deglaze the pan and remove all the fond that is
stuck to the bottom of that pan.
Fond is that goodness on the bottom of the pan when roasting something that adds a lot of flavor to your recipe.
The gravy will not be extremely thick, so feel free to remove the beef and stir in a 1/2 recipe of beurre manie over low
heat until it thickens.

- 4 cups water (OR can do half water, half beef broth)

- spaghetti noodles cooked
- beans
- onion diced
- cheddar cheese shredded
- oyster crackers

## Instructions
1. In a large dutch oven combine the water and tomato paste. Whisk together to combine.
2. Crumble the meat with fingers and add to the liquid in the pot.
3. Add all remaining ingredients to the pot and stir to combine.
4. Bring pot of chili to a simmer over medium heat. Cover and lower heat. Let simmer for 2-3 hours stirring occasionally. Skim grease
5. from the top as needed.
5. Remove the chili from the heat and allow to cool to room temperature. Cover and store the chili in the refrigerator overnight.
6. After chili has cooled overnight, using a spoon, breakup the grease on the top of the chili and remove completely.
7. Bring the chili back to a low simmer over medium heat.
8. Serve the chili warm over spagehtti noodles or over a hot dog.

## Notes
If you don't have time to store the chili overnight, you can simply skim the grease as best as you can from the top of the chili and serve.
Storing overnight helps remove the grease and allows further development of the flavors. It is not necessary.

ingredients: Salt and white pepper to taste
content:
# Classic Italian Lasagna

## Description
This traditional Italian lasagna features layers of pasta, rich meat ragù, creamy béchamel sauce, and Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese. The result is a hearty, flavorful dish perfect for family dinners or special occasions.

## Ingredients

### For the Meat Ragù
- 1 pound ground beef
- 1 pound Italian sausage
- 1 large onion, finely diced
- 2 carrots, finely diced
- 2 celery stalks, finely diced
- 4 garlic cloves, minced
- 2 (28 oz) cans whole peeled tomatoes
- 1 cup red wine
- 2 bay leaves
- 2 tablespoons tomato paste
- Salt and pepper to taste
- 2 tablespoons olive oil

### For the Béchamel Sauce
- 5 tablespoons butter
- 5 tablespoons all-purpose flour
- 4 cups whole milk
- 1/4 teaspoon nutmeg
- Salt and white pepper to taste

### For Assembly
- 1 pound lasagna noodles (fresh or dried)
- 2 cups freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano
- 1 pound fresh mozzarella, sliced thin

## Instructions

### Meat Ragù
1. Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add onion, carrots, and celery. Cook until softened (8-10 minutes).
2. Add garlic and cook until fragrant (1 minute).
3. Add ground beef and sausage. Break up meat and cook until browned (10 minutes).
4. Add wine and simmer until mostly evaporated (5 minutes).
5. Add tomatoes, tomato paste, and bay leaves. Break up tomatoes with spoon.
6. Simmer uncovered for 1.5-2 hours, stirring occasionally. Season with salt and pepper.

### Béchamel Sauce
1. Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
2. Add flour and whisk constantly for 2-3 minutes to make a roux.
3. Gradually add warm milk, whisking constantly to prevent lumps.
4. Cook until thickened (8-10 minutes), stirring frequently.
5. Add nutmeg, salt, and white pepper.

### Assembly
1. Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).
2. If using dried pasta, cook according to package directions.
3. In a 9x13 baking dish, spread a thin layer of ragù.
4. Layer in this order:
   - Pasta sheets
   - Meat ragù
   - Béchamel sauce
   - Parmigiano-Reggiano
   - Mozzarella slices
5. Repeat layers 3-4 times, ending with cheese on top.
6. Cover with foil and bake for 25 minutes.
7. Remove foil and bake additional 15-20 minutes until golden and bubbling.
8. Let rest 15-20 minutes before serving.

## Yield
8-10 servings

## Time
- Prep Time: 1 hour
- Cook Time: 2.5-3 hours
- Total Time: 3.5-4 hours

## Notes
- Make ragù a day ahead for better flavor
- For easier slicing, let lasagna rest at least 15 minutes after baking
- Fresh pasta sheets are traditional but dried work well too
- Freeze unbaked lasagna for up to 3 months
- Leftovers keep well refrigerated for 3-4 days

like seafood, replace with 2 large chicken thigh fillets.Chicken: Substitute with pork if desired.Rice: Medium grain
or jasmine rice yield the best results.Fire roasted peppers: Make your own by placing them on direct flame over a

By Melissa Clark
Total Time 2½ hours, plus marinating
Rating (5,081)
A coq au vin is a classic French stew in which chicken is braised slowly in red wine and a little brandy to yield a supremely rich sauce filled

# Cream of Chicken Soup Recipe

Cream of Chicken Soup Recipe - The Cozy Cook

## Overview
- **Total Time**: 5 mins 10 mins 15 mins
- **Servings**: 2 cans Calories

## Ingredients
- 4 Tablespoons Butter
- ½ cup + 2 Tablespoons Flour
- 2 cups Chicken Broth
- 1 chicken bouillon cube or 1 teaspoon Better Than Bouillon. (Optional- see notes.)
- 1 cup milk preferably whole but any kind works
- 1/3 teaspoon celery salt
- 1/3 teaspoon onion powder
- 1/3 teaspoon garlic powder
- 1/3 teaspoon salt
- 1/3 teaspoon pepper

## Instructions
1. Note: It’s important to whisk continuously throughout this process to ensure the smoothest
2. possible consistency.
2. Temper the milk by microwaving it for 45 seconds. This prevents curdling but also
3. prevents lumps from forming when it’s added. Set aside.
3. Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Let it fully melt and wait until it starts to
4. foam, about 3 minutes.
4. Gradually add the flour, whisk continuously for 3-5 minutes, until it’s the consistency of wet
5. sand. Remove from heat.
5. Add 1/3 of the chicken broth and whisk well. Add 1/3 more, whisk well.
6. Add the remaining chicken broth, chicken bouillon, warm milk, and seasonings, whisk
7. continuously.
7. Return to heat and bring to a near boil. Continue to whisk until it begins to get very thick.
8. Immediately remove from heat.
8. Soup will continue to thicken upon standing.
9. If possible, run the mixture through a fine mesh strainer for a super-smooth consistency.
10. Use as a direct substitute for condensed cream of chicken soup, this recipe makes enough
11. for two (10.5 oz.) cans.
12. Cream of Chicken Soup Recipe - The Cozy Cook

## Notes
Adding chicken bouillon to the mix help match the concentrated chicken flavor found in
condensed soups. This is especially helpful if store-bought chicken broth (such as Swanson), is
used instead of homemade chicken stock.
Reducing Sodium: You can use unsalted butter and reduced sodium chicken broth and bouillon
to lower the salt content. You can also refrain from adding salt as a seasoning.

# Croque Monsieur

Croque Monsieur - Tastes Better From Scratch

## Overview
- **Total Time**: 10 mins 20 mins 30 mins
- **Servings**: 4

## Ingredients
- Béchamel sauce:
- ¼ cup unsalted butter (½ stick)
- ¼ cup all-purpose flour
- 1½ cups whole milk
- salt and freshly ground black pepper
- 1/4 teaspoon dijon mustard
- dash of ground nutmeg
- Sandwich:
- 8 thin slices white sandwich breads
- 5 ounces good quality ham about 8 slices
- 6 ounces Gruyere cheese ,or Emmental cheese, grated (about 2½ cups)
- 1/4 cup freshly grated parmesan cheese

## Instructions
1. Béchamel sauce:
1. Melt butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in flour and cook, stirring
2. constantly, for about 3 minutes. Gradually add milk, stirring well until the mixture is smooth.
3. Cook, stirring, until sauce is thickened.
4. Croque Monsieur - Tastes Better From Scratch
2. Season with a little bit of salt and pepper. Remove from heat and whisk in mustard and
3. nutmeg. Set aside while you make the sandwiches, or make the sauce up to 1 week in
4. advance.
5. Assemble sandwiches:
1. Preheat oven to 425° F. Line a baking tray with parchement paper and set aside.
2. Spread each bread slice with a layer of béchamel, spreading it all the way to the edges. Place
3. 4 slices of bread, béchamel side up, on prepared baking sheet.
3. Top each with a piece of ham, a handful of gruyere, and a sprinkle of parmesan cheese. Place
4. remaining slices of bread on top, béchamel side up, then top with remaining gruyere and
5. parmesan cheese.
4. Bake at 425 degrees F for about 5-6 minutes, until cheese is melted, and then turn the oven
5. to broil and broil until the cheese on top is lightly golden, 2-4 minutes.

## Notes
Cheese: Emmental cheese is often used for croque monsieur, but I found that hard to find, and I
do know Gruyere is commonly used as well, so either will work.
Béchamel: Save on prep time by making the white sauce ahead of time. Make it as instructed,
allow it to cool, place plastic wrap directly onto surface, then cover and refrigerate for up to 1
week.
Croque Madame: To make this into a Croque Madame sandwich, make the recipe as instructed,
then fry eggs (one for each sandwich, sunny-side up) in a separate skillet while the sandwiches
toast in the oven. Place an egg on top each sandwiches.

# Duck a L_Orange

Classic French Duck a L'Orange - Hunter Angler Gardener Cook

## Overview
- **Total Time**: 20 mins 1 hr 40 mins 2 hrs
- **Servings**: 4 people Author

## Ingredients
- 2 fat ducks, like mallards or pintail
- Salt
- 3 tablespoons sugar
- 1/4 cup red wine vinegar
- 2 cups duck stock or beef stock
- 4 sweet oranges
- 1 tablespoon arrowroot or corn starch
- 3 tablespoons Grand Marnier or other orange liqueur
- 1/4 teaspoon orange bitters (optional)
- 2 tablespoons room temperature butter

## Instructions
1. Use a needle or sharp knife point to pierce the skin of the fat ducks all over, taking care to not pierce the meat itself; go in at an
2. angle. This helps the fat render out of the bird. Salt the ducks well and preheat the oven to 325°F.
2. Put the ducks in an ovenproof pan. I rest them on celery leaves to prop them above the level of the pan; this helps them crisp
3. better. If you want, surround the duck with some root vegetables. Roast for 90 minutes.
3. Take the pan out and increase the heat to 425°F. When it hits this temperature, put the birds back in the oven and roast until the
4. skin is crispy, about 15 to 20 minutes.
4. Meanwhile, boil the vinegar and sugar in a small pot until it turns brown. Pour in the stock little by little, stirring all the while. Set
5. aside.
6. Classic French Duck a L'Orange - Hunter Angler Gardener Cook
5. Shave the peel off the oranges, grating some fine and keeping the peel of 2 oranges in large pieces. Juice 2 oranges. Cut segments
6. from the other 2 oranges. Here is a tutorial on how to do that.
6. When the ducks are ready, remove them from the oven and let them rest on a cutting board.
7. Finish the sauce. Bring it to a simmer, then add about 1/2 cup of orange juice and the large bits of peel. Simmer 5 minutes. Whisk
8. together a little of the sauce with the starch, and, when it's mixed well, stir it into the saucepot to thicken. Add the Grand Marnier
9. and enough salt and orange bitters to taste. Swirl in the butter one tablespoon at a time.
8. To serve, carve the duck and arrange on plates. Give everyone some orange supremes and pour over the sauce. Garnish with the
9. grated zest, and serve with good bread, mashed potatoes or celery root, or polenta.

11. Store homemade hummus in an airtight container and refrigerate for up to one week. Freeze, covered with a thin layer of olive oil, for up to one month.
12. ADAM AND JOANNE'S TIPS
13. How to cook dried chickpeas: Use canned or home-cooked chickpeas for this recipe. Here is how we cook dried chickpeas.
14. Hummus without tahini: For the best hummus, which rivals our favorite store brands, use tahini. However, a chickpea puree without it is still quite delicious. Just
15. add more olive oil. Another option is to use natural, unsweetened, creamy peanut butter in its place.
16. If you like garlicky hummus, increase the garlic by a clove or use roasted garlic.
17. Aquafaba for fluffy hummus: This is the thick starchy liquid in a can of beans (or the bean cooking liquid). You can use this instead of water in the last step of the
18. recipe. Instead of plain water, add a splash of aquafaba at the end. As it whips, it creates an incredibly light and airy texture. Taste your aquafaba first. If it’s too salty,
19. use less salt when making your hummus.
20. Tahini & lemon juice are not creaming: Depending on your food processor, the blade might not come into contact with the tahini and lemon juice. You need to
21. increase the amount of liquid in the food processor, so add the olive oil. If they still do not cream, add a tablespoon of cold water.
22. Blender: A food processor is best for making hummus, but a high-powered blender will work. Be sure to scrape the sides down a few extra times as you make it.

## Instructions
1. Bring the chicken stock to a simmer in a medium soup pot. Stir in the sesame oil, salt, sugar,
2. white pepper, and MSG (if using). Add in the turmeric or 5 drops of yellow food coloring, if
3. using. This will give the soup that rich restaurant-style yellow color, but it is optional. Taste the
4. soup, and adjust the seasoning if needed.
2. Next add the cornstarch and water mixture. Make sure the cornstarch and water is mixed well,
3. as the cornstarch settles very quickly. Stir the soup continuously as you drizzle in the slurry, or
4. you'll get clumps of cooked starch in your soup. Use more or less starch if you like a thicker or
5. Egg Drop Soup - The Woks of Life
6. thinner soup. You can also add the starch in a couple small batches, let the soup simmer for a
7. couple of minutes, then check to see if the consistency is to your liking.
3. Now we're ready for the most exciting part: the egg. This recipe calls for the egg to be lightly
4. beaten, which results in both white and yellow egg swirls. The speed at which you stir the
5. soup when adding the egg also determines whether you get large “egg flowers” or small egg
6. flowers (i.e. swirly bits of egg). Use a ladle to stir the soup in a circular motion, and slowly

# Eggs Benedict with homemade Hollandaise Sauce

Eggs Benedict with homemade Hollandaise Sauce - Tastes Better From Scratch

## Overview
- **Total Time**: 10 mins 25 mins 35 mins
- **Servings**: 4 people Calories

## Ingredients
- 2 English muffins
- 4 large eggs
- 4 slices Canadian bacon
- Vinegar , just a splash

**For the Hollandaise sauce:**
- 4 Tablespoons butter
- 4 egg yolks
- 2 teaspoons lemon juice , or lime juice
- 1 Tablespoon heavy whipping cream
- salt and pepper (to taste)

## Instructions
1. For the Hollandaise sauce:
1. Melt the butter in a small saucepan. In a separate small bowl, beat the egg yolks. Mix in
2. lemon juice, whipping cream, and salt and pepper.
2. Add a small spoonful of the hot melted butter to the egg mixture and stir well. Repeat this
3. process adding a spoonful at a time of hot butter to the egg mixture.( Adding the butter
4. slowly, a spoonful at a time, will temper the eggs and ensure they don't curdle).
3. Once the butter has been incorporated, pour the mixture back into the saucepan. Cook on
4. low heat, stirring constantly, for just 20-30 seconds. Remove from heat and set aside. It will
5. thicken as it cools. Stir well and add another splash of cream, if needed, to thin.
6. To poach the eggs:
1. Fill a medium size pot with about 3 inches of water. Bring the water to a boil and then reduce
2. heat until it reaches a simmer. You should see small bubbles coming to the surface but not
3. Eggs Benedict with homemade Hollandaise Sauce - Tastes Better From Scratch
4. rolling.
2. Add a little splash of vinegar to the water (this is optional, but it helps the egg white to stay
3. together once it is in the water).
3. Crack one egg into a small cup (I use a measuring cup). Lower the egg into the simmer water,
4. gently easing it out of the cup.
4. Cook the egg in simmering water for 3-5 minutes, depending on how soft you want your egg
5. yolk. Remove the poached egg with a slotted spoon.
5. **It is not abnormal for a white foam to form on top of the water when poaching an egg. You
6. can simple skim the foam off of the water with a spoon.
6. While the egg is cooking, place the slices of Canadian bacon in a large pan and cook on
7. medium-high heat for about 1 minute on each side.
8. To Assemble:
1. Toast the English muffin. Top each toasted side with a slice or two of Canadian bacon, and
2. then a poached egg. Top with hollandaise sauce.

title: French-Style Beef Back Rib (Côtes de Boeuf)
filename: French-Style Beef Back Rib (Côtes de Boeuf)
description: A classic French preparation of beef back ribs, braised in red wine with aromatic vegetables and herbs, served with sweet mashed potatoes and coleslaw.
ingredients: Salt and freshly ground black pepper
3 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
Salt and white pepper to taste
content:
A classic French preparation of beef back ribs, braised in red wine with aromatic vegetables and herbs, served with sweet mashed potatoes and coleslaw.

# Ingredients

## For the Ribs
- 4-5 lbs beef back ribs
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 2 cups dry red wine (preferably Burgundy)
- 4 cups beef stock
- 2 large carrots, roughly chopped
- 2 celery stalks, roughly chopped
- 1 large onion, quartered
- 6 garlic cloves, crushed
- 2 bay leaves
- 4 sprigs fresh thyme
- 2 sprigs fresh rosemary
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper

## For the Sweet Mashed Potatoes
- 3 large sweet potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1/2 cup heavy cream
- 4 tbsp butter
- Salt and white pepper to taste
- Pinch of nutmeg

## For the Coleslaw
- 1/2 head green cabbage, finely shredded
- 2 carrots, julienned
- 1/4 red onion, thinly sliced
- 1/2 cup mayonnaise
- 2 tbsp Dijon mustard
- 2 tbsp white wine vinegar
- 1 tbsp honey
- Salt and pepper to taste

# Instructions

## Preparing the Ribs
1. Preheat oven to 325°F (165°C)
2. Season ribs generously with salt and pepper
3. Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat
4. Sear ribs until well-browned on all sides (about 3-4 minutes per side)
5. Remove ribs and set aside
6. In the same pot, add vegetables and sauté until softened
7. Add wine, scraping bottom to deglaze
8. Return ribs to pot, add stock and herbs
9. Bring to simmer, cover, and transfer to oven
10. Braise for 2.5-3 hours until meat is very tender

## Sweet Mashed Potatoes
1. Boil sweet potatoes until tender (20-25 minutes)
2. Drain well and return to pot
3. Add cream, butter, salt, pepper, and nutmeg
4. Mash until smooth and creamy

## Coleslaw
1. Mix cabbage, carrots, and onion in a large bowl
2. Whisk together mayonnaise, mustard, vinegar, and honey
3. Toss with vegetables
4. Season with salt and pepper
5. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour before serving

# Assembly and Serving
1. Remove ribs from braising liquid
2. Strain liquid and reduce by half for sauce
3. Serve ribs with reduced sauce
4. Plate with sweet mashed potatoes and coleslaw

# Notes
- For best results, prepare ribs a day ahead and reheat in braising liquid
- The coleslaw can be made up to 24 hours in advance
- Choose a good quality red wine that you would also drink
- For extra richness, finish sauce with a pat of cold butter

# Yield
Serves 4-6 people

# Time
- Prep: 45 minutes
- Cook: 3 hours
- Total: 3 hours 45 minutes
