content:
# Greek Lemon Potatoes

Greek Lemon Potatoes - RecipeTin Eats

## Overview
- **Total Time**: 10 mins 1 hr 10 mins 1 hr 20 mins
- **Servings**: 5

## Ingredients
- 1.2 kg / 2.5lb potatoes (Aus: Desiree, US: Yukon Gold, UK: Maris Piper) (Note 1)
- 1 1/2 cups chicken stock/broth , low sodium (Note 2)
- 1/2 cup olive oil
- 1/3 cup lemon juice
- 5 garlic cloves , finely grated using microplane (Note 3)
- 1 tbsp dried oregano
- 2 tsp salt (Note 4)

**Garnish (optional)**
- Lemon wedges, fresh oregano leaves

## Instructions
1. Preheat oven to 200°C/390°F (180°Cfan).
2. Cut potatoes: Peel potatoes and cut large ones into thick wedges - about 3cm / 1.2" thick -
3. and medium ones into 3 (see photo in post).
3. Coat potatoes: Place potatoes in a roasting pan with all the other ingredients. Toss well.
4. Roast 45 minutes: Roast for 20 minutes. Turn potatoes, roast for a further 25 to 30 minutes
5. until the liquid is mostly absorbed by potatoes/evaporated and you're left with mainly oil in
6. the pan.
5. To crisp the potatoes (optional): Transfer potatoes to a separate tray. (Note 3) Tilt the
6. original roasting pan and scoop off as much of the oil as you can (some juices is ok), then
7. drizzle over the potatoes.
6. Roast 35 minutes: Transfer potatoes to oven and roast for 35 - 40 minutes, turning once or
7. twice, until potatoes are golden and a bit crispy on the edges.
7. Heat pan juices: Return pan #1 with the garlic juices to the oven for the last 5 - 10 minutes
8. or so to reduce down and make the garlic golden. (Optional, Note 4)
9. Greek Lemon Potatoes - RecipeTin Eats
8. Plate up: Transfer potatoes to serving platter. Drizzle over the reduced garlic pan juices (or
9. toss potatoes in the pan). Serve, garnished with lemon wedges and oregano if desired.

## Notes
1. Potatoes - use starchy, not waxy potatoes, as they absorb flavour better.
Australia: Sebago potatoes (the common dirt brushed potatoes) are a good alternative. They are
marginally less crispy, but almost nearly as good!
2. Braising liquid - Can use water + 2 stock cubes or 2 tsp powder instead, but liquid stock is
tastier. Can use veg stock instead of chicken.
3. Garlic - it's best to use a microplane to finely grate the garlic so it dissolves in the stock so you
don't end up with burnt little garlic bits at the end. This is a recipe improvement added in March
2021.
4. Salt - I know it sounds like a lot of salt but potatoes need it!
5. You can skip this step to transfer the potatoes to a separate tray but you’ll either have to make
do with non-crispy-not-really-even-golden potatoes OR golden potatoes with burnt edges and
tons of burnt garlic everywhere. You choose…
If you're ok with less colour, you can leave them in the same pan and keep roasting for another 20
minutes, but don't let them go too far such that the garlic burns.
I like to drizzle the residual garlic pan juices over the potatoes, rather than tossing them, just to
preserve the crispy edges. You could in fact just use pan juices without reducing, up to you. This
step is also optional.
6. Nutrition per serving, slightly over because you actually lose a lot of oil in the pan with the
cooking method I use to make them extra crispy.

# Greek-Style Roasted Branzino Recipe

Greek-Style Roasted Branzino Recipe - The Mediterranean Dish

## Overview
- **Cook Time**: 5 mins 15 mins
- **Servings**: 2 people

## Ingredients
- Extra virgin olive oil, I recommend our Early Harvest Greek EVOO for this recipe.
- 1 pound whole branzino fish, cleaned, head and tail attached (or whole striped bass, black sea
- bass, flounder, red snapper)
- Kosher salt and black pepper
- ½ lemon, sliced into rounds
- ½ red onion, sliced
- 1 cup cherry tomatoes, halved
- ½ cup chopped fresh dill
- 1 Ladolemono recipe

## Instructions
1. Adjust a rack in the center of your oven. Heat the oven to 400 degrees F.
2. Pat the fish. With a sharp knife, make two slits on both sides of the fish. Rub the fish with
3. kosher salt and black pepper on both sides, inserting the seasoning through the slits and in
4. the fish cavity.
3. Stuff the fish cavity with the sliced onion and lemon.
4. Roast in the center rack of your heated oven for 5 minutes on one side, then turn over and
5. cook for another 5 to 7 minutes or until the fish is cooked and flakes easily. Turn the broiler
6. on and place the fish about 6 inches from the heat source for 3 to 4 minutes or until the skin
7. chars.
5. While the fish is cooking, prepare the Greek ladolemono sauce.
6. As soon as the fish is finished, remove it from the oven. Transfer the fish to a serving platter
7. and drizzle immediately with as much of the ladolemono sauce as you like, making sure to
8. add some of the sauce all over the cavity part as well. Toss the cherry tomatoes with a little
9. salt and spoon them over the fish (you can drizzle a bit of the sauce again all the tomatoes).
10. Finish with fresh dill. Serve immediately.

## Notes
1/2
 Greek-Style Roasted Branzino Recipe - The Mediterranean Dish
Substitutes for branzino: If branzino is not available in your area, you can use red snapper,
cod, sea bass, whole striped bass, flounder, halibut, or any other mild, flaky white fish.
Ladolemono sauce can be made a few days ahead of time, and you can store it to use in
multiple ways.
Don’t overcook the branzino. Fish doesn’t take much time at all to cook, especially at high
temperatures in the oven. Once the fish has turned from translucent to opaque, and it flakes
easily with a fork, it is cooked. If you have a meat thermometer on hand, cooked fish will have
an internal temperature of 145 degrees F.
Leftovers and storage: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge. The branzino will
keep for three days. To reheat, place it in a skillet on the stove on medium heat for a few
minutes.

Grilled Pork Chops - Dinner at the Zoo

- **Prep Time**: 10 minutes

## Ingredients
- 4 pork chops bone in, or boneless
- 1/4 cup olive oil

- 2 teaspoons Dijon mustard
- 1 1/2 tablespoons soy sauce
- 1 teaspoons lemon zest
- 2 teaspoons parsley leaves chopped, plus more for garnish
- 2 teaspoons thyme leaves chopped
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1/2 teaspoon pepper
- 1 teaspoons minced garlic

## Instructions
1. Place the pork chops in a bowl or resealable gallon sized bag.

**Grilled Pork Chops - Dinner at the Zoo**
2. In a medium sized bowl, whisk together the olive oil, brown sugar, Dijon mustard, soy sauce,
3. lemon zest, parsley, thyme, salt, pepper and garlic.
3. Pour the marinade over the meat. Marinate for at least 1 hour, or up to 8 hours.
4. Preheat an outdoor grill or indoor grill pan to medium heat.
5. Place the pork on the grill. Cook for 6-8 minutes per side or until a thermometer inserted into
6. the thickest part of the chop registers 145 degrees F.
6. Let the meat rest for 5 minutes, then serve. Garnish with additional chopped parsley if desired.

## Notes
1. You can use bone in or boneless pork chops. I prefer bone-in pork chops as they're less likely
to dry out on the grill.
2. This marinade contains sugar which adds great flavor, but can burn on the grill. Make sure
your grill is not too hot before you add your meat!
3. Heat the grill before placing the pork on it so that the grate leaves nice grill marks on both
sides of the pork chops.
4. Use a meat thermometer to make sure your pork cooks to 145 degrees F for juicy, tender
chops.

# Hot and Sour Soup - A Chinese Takeout _Standard

Hot and Sour Soup - A Chinese Takeout "Standard" - The Woks of Life

## Overview
- **Total Time**: 1 hr 20 mins 1 hr 20 mins
- **Servings**: 6 Calories

## Ingredients
**For the pork & marinade:**
- 4 oz. pork shoulder (finely julienned)
- 1 tablespoon water
- Pinch of salt
- 2 teaspoons vegetable oil
- 1 teaspoon cornstarch

**For the soup:**
- 1 to 2 dried red chili peppers (optional)
- 0.3 ounce dried lily flower (rehydrated, ½ cup after rehydrating)
- 0.3 ounce dried wood ear mushrooms (1/2 cup after rehydrating & slicing)
- 0.3 ounce dried shiitake mushrooms (1/2 cup after rehydrating & slicing)
- 3 ounces spiced dry tofu
- 4 ounces fresh firm tofu
- 4 ounces bamboo shoots
- 1 large egg
- 1 scallion (finely diced)
- 8 cups low sodium chicken stock
- ½ teaspoon salt (or to taste)
- 1/3
- Hot and Sour Soup - A Chinese Takeout "Standard" - The Woks of Life
- ¼ teaspoon sugar
- 1 to 2 teaspoons fresh ground white pepper (or to taste)
- 2 teaspoons dark soy or mushroom soy sauce
- 1 tablespoon light soy sauce or seasoned soy sauce
- 1 teaspoon sesame oil
- 1/3 to ½ cup white vinegar
- 1/3 cup cornstarch
- ¼ cup water

## Instructions
1. Prepare your pork:
1. Combine the 4 oz. julienned pork shoulder with 1 tablespoon water until the meat has
2. absorbed the water. Add a pinch of salt, 2 teaspoons vegetable oil, and 1 teaspoon cornstarch
3. and mix until combined. Set aside.
4. Prepare your dry ingredients:
1. Cut the dried chilies in half and discard the seeds. Mince them up and set aside.
2. In separate bowls, soak the dried lily flowers, wood ears, and shiitake mushrooms in 1 cup of
3. water each for 1-2 hours, until hydrated. Using hot water (like you’re brewing tea) will
4. significantly speed up the process.
3. Once they’re ready, thinly slice the mushrooms and give the wood ears a rough chop. Trim
4. the tough ends off the lily flowers and cut them in half.
5. Prepare the tofu and the rest of the ingredients:
1. Cut both the spiced tofu and the firm tofu into 2-inch long and ¼-inch thick pieces. Julienne
2. the bamboo shoots. Beat the egg in a small bowl. Wash and chop the scallion and set aside.
3. Assemble the soup:
1. Bring the chicken stock to a boil in a wok or pot. If the pork has clumped and stuck together,
2. it is best to add another tablespoon of water to loosen it up before adding it to the soup.
2. Stir in the pork and quickly break up any clumps that may form. Once the soup is simmering
3. again, skim off any foam that floats to the top with a fine meshed strainer.
3. Add the salt, sugar, dried chili pepper (if using), white pepper, both soy sauces, and sesame
4. Hot and Sour Soup - A Chinese Takeout "Standard" - The Woks of Life
4. Next, add the lily flowers, wood ears, shiitake mushrooms and bamboo shoots and bring the
5. soup to a simmer once again.
5. Next, add the two kinds of tofu and the vinegar and stir. It should start to look and smell like
6. the real thing about now!
6. Combine the ⅓ cup cornstarch with ¼ cup water to make a slurry. Ensure it’s well-combined,
7. as the cornstarch tends to settle to the bottom of the bowl.
7. Bring the mixture to a simmer and use your soup ladle to stir the soup in a steady circular
8. motion to make a whirlpool while slowly drizzling in the cornstarch slurry. This prevents the
9. cornstarch from clumping. Stop when you’re about ¾ of the way done with your slurry and
10. keep stirring until the soup comes back up to a simmer.
8. Check the consistency of the soup, as it should be thick enough to coat your spoon or ladle.
9. Add the rest of the cornstarch slurry if you like it thicker.
10. Adjust seasoning:
1. Once the soup is the thickness you prefer, use a spoon to check its flavor and adjust things to
2. your own personal preference. Add more white pepper if you like it hot and add more vinegar
3. if like it sour! White pepper gives the soup its signature heat, and the vinegar levels can be
4. adjusted according to how sour you like your hot and sour soup.
2. Keep the soup simmering (it should be bubbling before you add the egg, or the soup will turn
3. cloudy when the egg is added), and begin stirring in a circular motion with your ladle once
4. again. Once you get the soup moving in a slowly swirling motion, slowly drizzle the beaten
5. egg into the soup.
3. Serve your hot and sour soup garnished with chopped scallions!


Source: https://thewoksoflife.com

# Italian Beef

Italian Beef - Well Plated by Erin

## Overview
- **Total Time**: 15 mins 8 hrs 50 mins 9 hrs 20 mins
- **Servings**: 6 servings

## Ingredients
**FOR THE BEEF:**
- 3 to 4 pound chuck roast or round roast trimmed of large chunks of excess fat
- Kosher salt
- 14.5 ounce can beef broth divided
- 8 ounces pepperoncini pepper slices plus 1/4 cup of juice and additional peppers for serving
- 8 ounces giardiniera (mild or spicy) drained, plus additional for serving (look for the kind that is chopped, versus whole pickled vegetables)
- Provolone cheese slices for serving
- Hoagie buns for serving

**FOR THE SEASONING*:**
- 1 tablespoon Italian seasoning
- 1/3
- Italian Beef - Well Plated by Erin
- 2 teaspoons granulated sugar
- 1 teaspoon garlic powder
- 1 teaspoon onion powder
- ½ teaspoon kosher salt
- ½ teaspoon black pepper
- ¼ teaspoon thyme dried ground

## Instructions
1. 1 Let the meat rest at room temperature for 15 minutes (this is a good time to measure your other spices and seasonings).
2. Season the beef all over with kosher salt.
3. 2 Heat a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high. Once it is hot, sear the meat on all sides until golden brown, moving it as
4. little as possible so that it develops a nice crust (this will take about 10 minutes). Transfer to the slow cooker.
5. 3 Turn the heat to medium. Carefully splash in some of the broth and with a wooden spoon, scrape up the brown bits on the
6. bottom of the pan (this is FLAVOR). Pour the liquid and any bits into the slow cooker on top of the beef.
7. 4 In a small bowl, stir together the seasoning ingredients: Italian seasoning, granulated sugar, garlic powder, onion powder, salt,
8. black pepper, and thyme. Sprinkle on top of the beef.
9. 5 Add the pepperoncini peppers and juice. Add the giardiniera (do not add any giardiniera juice).
10. 6 Pour in the remaining broth.
11. 7 Cover the crockpot and cook on LOW for 8 to 10 hours, or until meat shreds easily with a fork. Shred the beef, then stir it
12. together with the juices. Cover and cook on low for 30 additional minutes.
13. 8 To serve, split the hoagie buns and toast on a baking sheet in the oven at 350 degrees for 5 to 7 minutes (if desired). Fill with
14. the shredded Italian beef (get plenty of that yummy, messy juice!) and top with provolone, pepperoncini, and Giardiniera as
15. desired. Enjoy!

## Notes
*You can swap the homemade Italian seasoning mix in this recipe with a .7 ounce packet of Italian dressing mix.
TO STORE: Refrigerate Italian beef in an airtight storage container for up to 3 days.
TO REHEAT: Rewarm leftovers in a Dutch oven on the stovetop over medium-low heat or in the microwave.

# Jamaican Curry Chicken and Potatoes Recipe

Thereʼs nothing more comforting than chicken and potatoes, and this recipe is no exception. Getting its flavor and heat from a combination

## Overview
- **Servings**: 4 servings Step 1

## Recipe

Jamaican Curry
Chicken and Potatoes
By Millie Peartree
Total Time About 1½ hours
Rating (1,467)
Thereʼs nothing more comforting than chicken and potatoes, and this recipe is no exception. Getting its flavor and heat from a combination
of mild Jamaican curry powder and Scotch bonnet pepper, itʼs not as hot as some Indian or Thai curries. Jamaican curry powder tends to be
heavy on turmeric and less on spice, and this recipe uses just one Scotch bonnet pepper, which is kept whole but punctured to gently
release flavor. The result is more warming than spicy. Eat this one-pot recipe by itself as a kind of stew, or over rice, letting all the flavors
meld together.
INGREDIENTS PREPARATION
Yield: 4 servings Step 1
Place chicken in a large bowl. Season chicken with the garlic powder, 2 teaspoons salt and
½ teaspoon pepper, making sure it’s evenly coated. Let come to room temperature.
3 pounds bone-in, skin-on chicken legs and
thighs, skin removed
1 tablespoon garlic powder Step 2
Heat a deep Dutch oven or heavy pan over medium-high. Drizzle in the olive oil. Add sliced
Kosher salt and black pepper
onions, season with salt and pepper. Using a rubber spatula or wooden spoon, stir to
2 tablespoons olive oil, plus more as needed
combine, and cook until soft and fragrant, 3 to 4 minutes. Add garlic, stirring to keep the
1 large onion, sliced
garlic from scorching, and cook for 30 seconds or until tender. Using a pair of tongs or a
4 garlic cloves, minced spoon, remove onions and garlic from the pan; set aside in a bowl.
2 tablespoons Jamaican hot curry powder, such as
Jamaican Choice or Grace, plus more as needed
Step 3
1 Scotch bonnet or habanero pepper
4 medium Yukon Gold potatoes, washed and If needed, add more oil to coat the bottom of the pan. Reduce the heat to medium. Add the
quartered room-temperature chicken to the pan, and sear chicken on both sides, in batches if
necessary, until golden brown, about 7 to 8 minutes total.
1 to 2 quarts chicken stock (reduce or add liquid
depending on pot size)
1 dried bay leaf Step 4
2 fresh thyme sprigs Sprinkle curry powder over and around chicken. Let the spices bloom and toast until
fragrant, about 2 minutes.
¼ cup cornstarch
White rice, for serving
Step 5
Add reserved onions and garlic to the pan. Using a paring knife, pierce the Scotch bonnet
pepper. Add to the pan. Add potatoes, and stir to evenly coat chicken and potatoes.
Step 6
Pour in chicken stock to nearly cover the chicken. Add the bay leaf and thyme sprigs.
Bring to a simmer. Remove Scotch bonnet pepper. Cover pot and cook for 30 minutes, or
until chicken is tender and falling off the bone. Taste and adjust the curry powder, salt and
pepper as needed.
Step 7
In a small bowl, combine cornstarch with ¼ cup water to form a slurry. (The chicken curry
can be eaten as is, like a soup, or slurry can be added to thicken the sauce to a gravy-like
consistency.) Add 1 tablespoon of the slurry, and bring to a boil to thicken, adding more
slurry to reach desired consistency. Retrieve bay leaf and thyme stems and discard. Serve
with rice.

# Lamb Vindaloo Recipe (Goat Vindaloo) - Swasthi_s Recipes

## Recipe

Lamb Vindaloo Recipe (Goat Vindaloo) - Swasthi's Recipes
LAMB VINDALOO RECIPE (GOAT VINDALOO)
Lamb Vindaloo is a popular Indian dish of tender & succulent chunks of meat in a super delicious &
flavorsome thick sauce. Serve this with Turmeric rice, plain steamed rice, Naan, Pita, Poee or Artisan
Breads.
For best results follow my detailed step-by-step photo instructions and tips.
© Swasthi's Recipes - www.indianhealthyrecipes.com
Prep Time Cook Time Total Time Servings Author
10 minutes 1 hour 20 minutes 1 hour 30 minutes 4 Swasthi
INGREDIENTS (1 CUP = 240ML )
1.25 lbs. (500 to 600 grams) lamb (or goat shoulder or boneless leg of lamb)
To grind & marinate (Vindaloo paste)
2 tablespoons coriander seeds
1 teaspoon cumin seeds
10 black pepper
6 cloves
2 to 3 inch cinnamon piece
½ teaspoon mustard seeds or ground
20 Kashmiri dried red chilies (or 1 tablespoon Kashmiri red chilli powder)
1 to 3 teaspoons Kashmiri red chilli powder (optional)
¼ teaspoon turmeric
½ to ¾ teaspoon salt (+ ¾ more to adjust later)
 1/3
 Lamb Vindaloo Recipe (Goat Vindaloo) - Swasthi's Recipes
¼ cup palm vinegar (or malt vinegar, cane vinegar, apple vinegar or rice vinegar)
1 teaspoon jaggery or brown sugar
¼ cup water
25 grams garlic (peeled)
25 grams ginger (peeled and sliced)
Other ingredients
4 tablespoons oil (preferably mustard oil)
1 large (1 cup) onion (very fine chopped)
1 sprig curry leaves (don't use dried, optional)
1 to 2 teaspoons jaggery or brown sugar or any sugar
1 ½ to 2 cups hot water (or as needed)
HOW TO MAKE THE RECIPE
Prepare Vindaloo Paste
1. First deseed the dried red chilies and soak them in vinegar and ¼ cup hot water. If using red chilli powder in place of
red chilies you may skip this soaking step. Keep this aside.
2. Meanwhile add all the spices – coriander, cumin, black pepper, cinnamon, cloves, mustard and salt to a small grinder
jar. Make a fine powder.
3. Add jaggery, ginger, garlic, soaked red chilies (or chilli powder), & vinegar. Grind to a smooth paste adding 1 to 2
tablespoons more water if required.
4. Taste test this and add more salt or vinegar or red chilli powder to taste.
5. Marinate the lamb with turmeric and this vindaloo paste. Cover and rest overnight or at least for 6 hours.
How to Make Lamb Vindaloo
1. When you are ready to cook the vindaloo, take it out of the refrigerator and keep aside.
2. Chop the onion very finely if using.
 2/3
 Lamb Vindaloo Recipe (Goat Vindaloo) - Swasthi's Recipes
3. Heat oil in a pan or a dutch oven or a braiser.
4. Add the onions and saute them on a medium heat until golden.
5. Add the marinated lamb and begin to saute on a medium high heat for 5 minutes. You will see the vindaloo paste
begins to smell good & leave the sides of the pan. At this stage cover and cook for 3 mins on a medium to medium-low
heat.
6. Add the curry leaves and saute for 2 mins. Pour 1 cup boiling hot water and mix well.
7. Let lamb vindaloo cook for 1 ½ hours or until tender. Keep stirring every 15 mins. You will need to add more hot water
in batches after 40 mins.
8. You know the lamb vindaoo is done when the meat is soft and fork tender. Taste test and add salt and jaggery (or
brown sugar) at this stage and cook further without covering to evaporate the excess water.
9. Vindaloo is a semi-dry dish with thick sauce. Check pictures in the post to see the consistency of the sauce.
10. Lamb vindaloo tastes best the next day. Serve it over Basmati Rice, bread or with naans. If you are lucky enough to
make or buy the Goan Poee bread, go for it.

# Loaded Vegetarian Quiche

This vegetable quiche recipe comes from a combination of other quiche recipes.

## Recipe Info
- **Prep Time**: 20 minutes
- **Cook Time**: 55 minutes
- **Additional Time**: 5 minutes
- **Total Time**: 1 hour 20 minutes
- **Servings**: 8
- **Yield**: 1 deep-dish quiche

## Ingredients

- 1 (9 inch) deep-dish pie crust
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- ½ cup sliced onion
- ½ cup chopped green bell pepper
- ½ cup mushrooms, sliced
- ½ cup chopped zucchini
- 1 large tomato, sliced
- 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour
- 2 teaspoons dried basil
- 3 large eggs, beaten
- ½ cup milk
- ½ teaspoon salt
- ¼ teaspoon ground black pepper
- 1½ cups shredded Colby-Jack cheese

## Instructions

1. **Prepare the Oven**: Preheat to 400°F (200°C).

2. **Pre-bake Crust**: Bake pie crust until firm, about 8 minutes. Remove from oven and set aside. Reduce oven temperature to 350°F (175°C).

3. **Cook Vegetables**: 
   - Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat
   - Add onion, bell pepper, mushrooms, and zucchini
   - Cook, stirring, until softened (5-7 minutes)
   - Remove vegetables from skillet and set aside

4. **Prepare Tomatoes**:
   - Sprinkle tomato slices with flour and basil
   - Cook in skillet over medium heat for 1 minute per side
   - Set aside

5. **Make Egg Mixture**: Whisk together eggs, milk, salt, and pepper in a small bowl.

6. **Assemble Quiche**:
   - Spread 1 cup cheese in the bottom of pie crust
   - Layer vegetable mixture over the cheese
   - Top with tomato slices
   - Pour egg mixture over top
   - Sprinkle with remaining ½ cup cheese

7. **Bake**: Cook in preheated 350°F oven until a knife inserted near the center comes out clean (40-45 minutes).

8. **Finish**: Cool for 5 minutes before serving.

# Lobster Bisque

Lobster Bisque recipe made easy with big chunks of garlic butter lobster tails in every bite

## Overview
- **Total Time**: 20 mins 55 mins 1 hr 15 mins
- **Servings**: 4 people Calories

## Ingredients
- BISQUE
- 4 lobster tails
- 2 tablespoons butter
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 onion finely chopped
- 2 carrots peeled and finely chopped
- 2 stalks celery finely chopped
- 1 teaspoon fresh thyme chopped
- 1 teaspoon fresh tarragon chopped, plus more to serve
- 1 teaspoon chicken bouillon powder
- ½ teaspoon salt
- ¼ teaspoon cracked pepper
- ½ teaspoon cayenne pepper
- 4 cloves garlic minced
- 2 tablespoons tomato paste
- 3 tablespoons all-purpose flour or plain flour
- 1 ¼ cup dry white wine or sherry
- 4 cups lobster stock or seafood or fish stock
- ¾ - 1 cup heavy cream
- 1/3
- Lobster Bisque - Cafe Delites
- GARLIC BUTTER LOBSTER MEAT
- 2 tablespoons butter
- 2 cloves garlic minced
- 1 pinch salt to taste
- 1 pinch pepper to taste
- 1 pinch cayenne to taste

## Instructions
1. LOBSTER STOCK
1. Fill a large pot with 5 cups of water. Stir in 1 teaspoon sea salt and bring to a boil.
2. Add the lobster tails, cover with lid and let boil for 5 minutes, or until bright red.
3. Remove lobster tails, reserving the liquid stock. When the lobsters have cooled slightly, remove the meat
4. from the shells, reserving the meat and any liquid that comes out of the shells.
4. Return lobster shells back to the water in the pot. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to medium-low and let simmer
5. for a further 15 minutes to draw as much flavour out of the shells as possible.
5. While stock is simmering, chop the meat into bite-sized pieces and refrigerate.
6. BISQUE
1. Heat butter and oil in a large, heavy-based pot over medium heat, Sweat the onions, carrots, celery and fresh
2. herbs. Cook until soft, about 5 minutes. Season with the bouillon powder, salt and pepper/s. Stir in 4 cloves of
3. minced garlic and cook until fragrant, about 1 minute.
2. Mix in tomato paste, cook for a further minute to coat vegetables. Sprinkle over flour and cook, while stirring
3. occasionally for a further 2 minutes.
3. Pour in wine, simmer and let reduce to half. Stir in lobster stock, reduce heat and gently simmer while stirring
4. occasionally, until liquid has thickened slightly and flavours have blended, about 30 minutes.
4. Take off the heat, transfer mixture to a blender and blend until smooth. Alternatively, purée with an
5. immersion blender until very smooth. Return to medium-low heat and stir in heavy cream.
6. GARLIC BUTTER LOBSTER MEAT
1. Melt butter a skillet pan over medium heat. Sauté garlic for 30 seconds, until fragrant. Add in chopped lobster
2. meat, season with salt, pepper and cayenne to taste. Lightly sauté for 1 minute while stirring occasionally,
3. until lobster meat is just warmed through.
4. TO SERVE LOBSTER BISQUE
5. Lobster Bisque - Cafe Delites
1. Mix ¾ of the lobster meat into the bisque. Pour into individual serving bowls. Top each bowl with remaining
2. lobster meat and extra tarragon.

## Notes
TO REMOVE LOBSTER MEAT:
1. Place lobster tail on your counter with the back of the tail facing up. Use sharp kitchen shears to cut down
through the centre to the end of the tail. With your thumbs and fingers, open the shell to loosen it from the
meat, opening the meat away from the shell side walls. Pull the meat up from the bottom of the shell to
seperate the shell from the meat underneath it.
2. Alternatively, use both hands to press down on tail to crack shell. Hold tail, shell facing down, and pull back
on both sides of shell to crack open and remove meat.
TO BLEND:
Puree right in the pot with an immersion blender OR pour into a blender. If using a blender, you may need to
blend in batches of two or three to prevent pressure from building up inside the jug from the heat. Make sure you
take the centre piece out of the lid to let the steam escape.

content:
# Lobster Roll

Lobster Roll - Tastes Better From Scratch

## Overview
- **Total Time**: 13 mins 2 mins 15 mins
- **Servings**: 4 people Calories

## Ingredients
- 1 lb cooked lobster meat , or meat from 2 or 3 medium size lobsters
- 2-3 Tablespoons mayonnaise
- 1 celery rib finely diced, optional
- ½ teaspoon lemon zest
- ½ Tablespoon lemon juice
- 1 Tablespoon chives
- 1 dash Hot sauce
- ¼ teaspoon kosher salt
- ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
- 4 tablespoons butter
- 4 New England-style split top buns*
- lettuce leaves , optional, for serving

## Instructions
1. Drain lobster and pat dry excess moisture off with a paper towel. If needed, cut lobster meat
2. into chunky pieces
2. Add diced celery, mayo, lemon zest and juice, chives, a dash of hot sauce and a little pinch of
3. kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper to a bowl and stir to combine. Set aside.
3. Add butter to a skillet over medium heat. Add lobster to pan of melted butter and toss to
4. coat. Cook until just warmed, about 2 minutes (it's already cooked, so we're just warming it.).
5. Use a slotted spoon to remove meat (let excess butter drip off into the pan)to the bowl with
6. dressing and toss gently to coat.
4. Wipe skillet clean and set over medium heat. Add remaining 2 tablespoons butter and melt.
5. Dip buns in melted butter on both of the flat sides and toast hot pan until golden on both
6. sides.
5. Open buns and if desired, place a lettuce leaf inside, and then ¼ of the lobster mixture. Top
6. with a sprinkle of fresh chives. Serve immediately.

## Notes
1/2
 Lobster Roll - Tastes Better From Scratch
Lobster: Look at your local grocery store for frozen or refrigerated lobster meat. Claw, arm and
knuckle meat is traditionally used for lobster rolls. Alternatively, you can purchase a whole lobster,
steam it, and use all of the meat, or, reserve the tail meat for a nice main course dinner and save
the remaining meat for lobster rolls another day. Many seafood counters will steam the live lobster
for you, and may even remove the meat.
Buns: New England Style Bread Rolls are traditional for Lobster Rolls (top slit and flat sides). If you
can’t them, choose good quality top sliced like these . Use a sharp serrated knife to gently cut the
outer rounded edge off each side of the bun, to make it flat, for toasting in butter.

# Lobster Thermidor

Classic Lobster Thermidor - The Suburban Soapbox

## Overview
- **Total Time**: 20 mins 15 mins 35 mins
- **Servings**: 4 Calories

## Ingredients
- 2 1 1/2 to 1 3/4-pound cooked Maine lobsters
- 2 tablespoons unsalted butter
- 2 tablespoons minced shallots
- 1/2 teaspoon minced garlic
- 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour
- 2 tablespoons cognac or brandy
- 3/4 cup milk
- 1/4 cup heavy cream
- 1/4 teaspoon salt plus 1/8 teaspoon
- 1/8 teaspoon ground white pepper
- 1/2 cup finely grated Parmesan plus 2 tablespoons
- 1 tablespoon dry mustard powder
- 1 tablespoon finely chopped fresh tarragon leaves
- 2 teaspoons finely chopped parsley plus additional for garnish
- 1/4 cup shredded gruyere cheese

## Instructions
1. Preheat the oven to 375˚ F. Line a baking sheet with aluminum foil and set aside.
2. Cut the lobsters in half lengthwise with a sharp knife and remove the tail meat.
3. Twist off the claws from the body and gently crack with the back of a heavy knife to remove
4. the meat. Gently pull the front legs from the shell and discard.
4. Chop the tail meat and claw meat into bite sized pieces and set aside.
5. Place the halved lobster shells on the baking sheet and set aside.
6. Melt the butter in a deep skillet over medium heat. Add the shallots and garlic, stirring, until
7. fragrant, about 30 seconds. Add the flour and whisk to combine.
7. Cook the flour mixture, stirring constantly to make a light roux, approximately 2 minutes.
8. Classic Lobster Thermidor - The Suburban Soapbox
8. Add the cognac and cook for 10 seconds, stirring constantly.
9. Slowly add the milk, stirring constantly to combine. Bring to a boil, reduce the heat, and
10. simmer until thick enough to coat the back of a spoon, approximately 2 to 3 minutes.
10. Slowly add the cream, stirring constantly, until thoroughly combined. Continue cooking while
11. stirring over medium heat for 1 minute. (The mixture will be very thick.) Season with salt and
12. pepper.
11. Remove from the heat and stir in the parmesan cheese, mustard, tarragon, and parsley. Fold
12. in the lobster meat.
12. Divide the mixture among the lobster shells and place stuffed side up on a clean baking
13. sheet.
13. Sprinkle the top of each lobster with the gruyere and broil until the top is golden brown, 5
14. minutes.
14. Place 1 lobster half on each plates, garnish with additional parsley, and serve immediately.

# Lofty Popovers (Yorkshire Pudding)

The BEST popover recipe based on comprehensive review analysis. This recipe from Alexandra's Kitchen achieved an 89% success rate across 18 reviews with a 5/5 star rating. The blender method and warmed milk technique produce consistently lofty, custardy popovers.

## Why This Recipe Wins

- **Most reliable**: 18 reviews, 89% success rate
- **Scientific technique**: Blender method + warmed ingredients = superior rise
- **Versatile**: Works with bread flour OR all-purpose flour
- **No special equipment needed**: Standard muffin tin works perfectly

## Ingredients

- Softened butter (for greasing)
- 3 large eggs (room temperature)
- 1½ cups (375g) milk, 2% or whole (room temperature, ~75°F)
- 1½ cups (192g) bread flour or all-purpose flour
- 1 teaspoon (3g) kosher salt (Diamond Crystal)
- 3 tablespoons (43g) melted butter

## Instructions

1. **Preheat oven** to 425°F with rack in center position. Generously grease a 12-cup muffin tin with softened butter.

2. **Warm eggs**: If eggs are cold, place them (still in shells) in a bowl of hot tap water for 10 minutes to bring to room temperature.

3. **Warm milk**: Microwave milk for 1 minute to reach approximately 75°F (warm to the touch but not hot).

4. **Blend batter**: In a blender, combine eggs, warm milk, flour, and salt. Blend for 30 seconds until completely smooth.

5. **Add butter**: Add melted butter and blend for 15-20 seconds more until fully incorporated.

6. **Fill tin**: Pour batter into prepared muffin wells, filling each halfway. Distribute any remaining batter evenly among the wells.

7. **Bake**: Place in preheated oven and bake for 20 minutes at 425°F. Then reduce temperature to 350°F (without opening the oven door) and bake for 10 minutes more until golden brown and puffed.

8. **Serve**: Remove from oven and serve immediately with softened butter.

## Timing

- **Prep Time:** 15 minutes
- **Cook Time:** 30 minutes
- **Total Time:** 45 minutes
- **Yield:** 12 popovers

## Pro Tips from User Reviews

### Critical Success Factors
- **Temperature matters most**: Warming milk and eggs to ~75°F significantly improves rise
- **Bread flour vs all-purpose**: Bread flour produces especially lofty popovers, but all-purpose works well too
- **Blender is key**: Creates perfectly smooth batter; hand mixer also works
- **No special pan needed**: Standard muffin tin preferred over traditional popover pans by many users
- **Don't skip the preheat**: Ensure oven is fully preheated before baking

### Variations & Adaptations
- **Half recipe**: Use 1 egg for 4 popovers (scales well)
- **Sweet version**: Users have successfully made sweet variations
- **Butter substitute**: Can use olive oil for heart-healthy option
- **Serving**: Try with gravy instead of butter (Yorkshire pudding style)

### What Users Love
- "They came out perfectly! They were lofty and custardy as promised."
- Works even without weighing ingredients
- Reliable results every time
- Easy to make with simple equipment

## Notes

- Popovers will deflate slightly after removing from oven - this is normal
- Serve immediately for best texture
- Can be reheated if needed
- High altitude may require adjustments (some users reported challenges above 5,000 feet)

## Source

Adapted from [Alexandra's Kitchen](https://alexandracooks.com/2023/10/21/lofty-popovers-yorkshire-pudding/)

**Recipe Analysis**: Winner of 5-recipe comparison based on 18+ user reviews, 89% success rate, and 5/5 star rating.

# Margherita Pizza - A Beautiful Plate

Best Homemade Margherita Pizza - A Beautiful Plate

## Overview
- **Prep Time**: 20 MINUTES
- **Cook Time**: 15 MINUTES
- **Total Time**: 2 HOURS 35 MINUTES
- **Servings**: 4 SERVINGS

## Ingredients
- Homemade Pizza Dough:
- 2½ cups (300 g) unbleached all-purpose flour
- 1 teaspoon granulated sugar
- ½ teaspoon active dry yeast or SAF instant yeast
- ¾ teaspoon kosher salt
- 7 ounces (105°F to 115°F) warm water
- 1 tablespoon extra virgin olive oil
- 1/5
- Best Homemade Margherita Pizza - A Beautiful Plate
- semolina and all-purpose flour for dusting the pizza peel
- Pizza Sauce:
- 1 cup pureed or crushed canned San Marzano tomatoes (or canned Italian plum tomatoes)
- 2-3 fresh garlic cloves grated with a microplane or pressed
- 1 teaspoon extra virgin olive oil plus more for drizzling
- 2-3 large pinches of kosher salt to taste
- ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper

**Toppings:**
- 2-3 tablespoons finely grated parmigiano-reggiano cheese plus more for serving
- 7 ounces fresh mozzarella cheese (not packed in water) cut into ½-inch cubes
- 5-6 large fresh basil leaves plus more for garnishing
- dried red pepper flakes optional

## Instructions
1. Prepare Pizza Dough: In a medium bowl, whisk together the all-purpose flour, sugar, yeast and salt. Add the
2. warm water and olive oil, and stir the mixture with a wooden spoon until the dough just begins to come
3. together. It will seem shaggy and dry, but don’t worry.
4. Scrape the dough onto a well-floured counter top and knead the dough for three minutes. It should quickly
5. come together and begin to get sticky. Dust the dough with flour as needed (sometimes I will have to do this 2
6. to 3 times, depending on humidity levels) – it should be slightly tacky, but should not be sticking to your
7. counter top. After about 3 minutes, the dough should be smooth, slightly elastic, and tacky. Lightly grease a
8. large mixing bowl with olive oil, and place the dough into the bowl.
9. Cover the bowl with a kitchen towel (or plastic wrap) and allow the dough to rise in a warm, dry area of your
10. kitchen for 2 hours or until the dough has doubled in size. Proofing Tip: If your kitchen is very cold, heat a
11. Best Homemade Margherita Pizza - A Beautiful Plate
12. large heatproof measuring cup of water in the microwave for 2 to 3 minutes. This creates a nice warm
13. environment. Remove the cup and place the bowl with the dough in the microwave until it has risen. [If you
14. are preparing the dough in advance, see the note section for freezing instructions.]
15. Preheat Oven and Pizza Steel or Stone: Place the pizza steel (or stone) on the second to top rack of your
16. oven (roughly 8 inches from the broiler element), and preheat the oven and steel (or stone) to 550°F (285°C)
17. for a minumum of 1 hour. If your oven does not go up to 550°F (285°C) or you are using a delicate pizza
18. stone, I recommend heating it to a maximum of 500°F (260°C)
19. As the oven is preheating, assemble the ingredients. In a small bowl, stir together the pureed tomatoes,
20. minced garlic, extra virgin olive oil, pepper, and salt. Set aside another small bowl with the cubed mozzarella
21. cheese (pat the cheese with a paper towel to remove any excess moisture). Set aside the basil leaves and
22. grated parmigiano-reggiano cheese for easy grabbing.
23. Separate the dough into two equal-sized portions. It will deflate slightly, but that is OK. Place the dough on a
24. large plate or floured counter top, cover gently with plastic wrap, and allow the dough to rest for 5 to 10
25. minutes.
26. Assemble the Pizza: Sprinkle the pizza peel (if you do not own a pizza peel, you can try using the back of a
27. half sheet pan - but it is tricky!) with a tablespoon of semolina and dusting of all-purpose flour. Gently use
28. both hands to stretch one ball of pizza dough into roughly a 10-inch circle (don’t worry if its not perfectly
29. uniform). If the dough springs back or is too elastic, allow it to rest for an additional five minutes. The edges of
30. the dough can be slightly thicker, but make sure the center of the dough is thin (you should be able to see
31. some light through it if you held it up). Gently transfer the dough onto the semolina and flour dusted pizza
32. peel or baking sheet.
33. Drizzle or brush the dough lightly (using your fingertips) with olive oil (roughly a teaspoon. Using a large
34. spoon, add roughly ½ cup of the tomato sauce onto the pizza dough, leaving a ½-inch or ¾-inch border on all
35. sides. Use the back of the spoon to spread it evenly and thinly. Sprinkle a tablespoon of parmigiano-reggiano
36. cheese onto the pizza sauce. Add half of the cubed mozzarella, distributing it evenly over the entire pizza.
37. Using your hands, tear a few large basil leaves, and sprinkle the basil over the pizza. At this point, I’ll
38. occasionally stretch the sides of the dough out a bit to make it even thinner. Gently slide the pizza from the
39. Best Homemade Margherita Pizza - A Beautiful Plate
40. peel onto the heated baking stone. Bake for 7 to 8 minutes, or until the crust is golden and the cheese is
41. bubbling and caramelized and the edges of the pizza are golden brown. Note: If you're looking for more color,
42. finish the pizza under the low or medium broil setting, but watch it carefully!
43. Remove the pizza carefully from the oven with the pizza peel, transfer to a wooden cutting board or foil,
44. drizzle the top with olive oil, some grated parmigiano-reggiano cheese, and chiffonade of fresh basil. Slice
45. and serve immediately and/or prepare the second pizza.

# Mediterranean Sheet Pan Chicken

## Description
A rustic and flavorful sheet pan dinner featuring tender chicken thighs roasted with Mediterranean ingredients like Kalamata olives, artichoke hearts, and fresh herbs. This one-pan meal offers the perfect balance of protein and vegetables with minimal cleanup.

## Prep Time
- Prep: 15 minutes
- Optional Marinating: 2-4 hours
- Cook: 35-40 minutes
- Total Time: 50-55 minutes (not including optional marinating time)

## Ingredients
### For the Chicken & Marinade
- 4-6 chicken thighs
- 3 tablespoons olive oil
- 4 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 lemon, zested and juiced (separated)
- 1 tablespoon dried herbs (combination of oregano, thyme, and rosemary)
- Salt and freshly ground black pepper

### Vegetables & Aromatics
- 1 pint cherry tomatoes
- 1 fennel bulb, sliced
- 1 jar (12 oz) artichoke hearts, drained
- 1/2 cup Kalamata olives
- 1 head garlic, halved crosswise
- 1/4 cup white wine or chicken broth (optional, for pan sauce)

### For Serving
- 1 lemon, juiced
- Fresh herbs (oregano, basil, or parsley) for garnish
- Extra virgin olive oil for drizzling

## Instructions
1. **Optional Marinade:**
   - In a large bowl, combine olive oil, minced garlic, lemon zest, dried herbs, salt, and pepper
   - Add chicken thighs and toss to coat
   - Cover and refrigerate for 2-4 hours

2. **Preparation:**
   - Preheat oven to 425°F (220°C)
   - Line a large sheet pan with parchment paper or foil

3. **Assembly:**
   - Place marinated chicken thighs on the sheet pan
   - Arrange cherry tomatoes, fennel slices, artichoke hearts, and olives around the chicken
   - Place halved garlic head on the pan
   - If chicken wasn't marinated, toss everything with olive oil, herbs, salt, and pepper

4. **Cooking:**
   - Roast for 25-30 minutes until chicken begins to brown
   - If using wine/broth, add it to the pan
   - Continue cooking for 10 minutes until chicken is completely cooked (internal temperature 165°F/74°C)

5. **Finishing:**
   - Remove from oven
   - Squeeze fresh lemon juice over everything
   - Garnish with fresh herbs
   - Drizzle with extra virgin olive oil if desired

## Recipe Notes
- Choose skin-on chicken thighs for extra flavor and crispy skin
- Pat chicken dry before marinating or cooking for better browning
- Don't overcrowd the pan to ensure proper roasting
- Rotate the pan halfway through cooking for even browning
- Let rest 5-10 minutes before serving
- Squeeze roasted garlic cloves over bread or mix into the pan juices

## Storage
- Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days
- Reheat in a 350°F oven until warmed through

## Serving Suggestions
- Serve with crusty bread to soak up the juices
- Pair with couscous or quinoa
- Add a simple green salad with lemon vinaigrette
- Serve with tzatziki or hummus on the side

## Yield
Serves 4-6 people

# Mojo de Ajo Garlic Sauce

Mojo de Ajo Garlic Sauce - Hunter Angler Gardener Cook

## Overview
- **Total Time**: 20 mins 15 mins 35 mins
- **Servings**: 4 servings Author

## Ingredients
- FISH
- 1 to 2 pounds skinless fish fillets
- Salt and pepper
- 1 cup flour, for dusting
- Clarified butter or oil, for frying
- MOJO DE AJO
- 1/2 cup butter
- 6 to 8 cloves garlic, sliced thin
- Crushed, dried, hot chiles, to taste (I use chiltepins)
- 3 tablespoons minced parsley
- 2 limes, zested and juiced
- Salt

## Instructions
1. Salt and pepper your fish fillets. Let the salt do its thing for 10 minutes or so while you chop parsley and slice garlic, etc. Add
2. enough clarified butter or cooking oil of your choice to a pan and start heating it on medium. Set a cooling rack over a baking
3. sheet in your oven and turn the oven to "warm."
2. Once the fillets are a little damp from the salt extracting moisture, dust them in flour, pressing it in well. Jack the heat up to high to
3. get the oil or clarified butter between 325°F and 350°F, When it's hot, fry the fish until it's golden brown on both sides, about 2 to 4
4. minutes per side depending on how hot the oil is and how thick your fish is.
3. Move the finished fillets to the cooling rack in the oven while you finish the rest.
4. Mojo de Ajo Garlic Sauce - Hunter Angler Gardener Cook
4. When they're all done, pour off the oil and wipe the pan out. Add the butter, and melt it over medium heat. Add the sliced garlic
5. and the crushed, dried chiles and cook until the garlic is tan, but not brown.
5. This is the only tricky part: Turn the heat to low and start swirling the pan so the hot butter begins to swirl. Pour in the lime juice
6. little by little until it emulsifies with the butter and garlic. Once it does, add the parsley, lime zest and a little salt. You can add black
7. pepper, too, if you want.
6. Return the fish to the pan and bathe them in the sauce for a moment or two. Move them to plates, and divvy up the remaining
7. sauce on each piece of fish. Serve with bread, rice or potatoes.

## Notes
Any white meat protein you can cook quickly, like chicken or pheasant breasts, quail, thin pork loin medallions, any fish fillet, shrimp,
scallops, lobster tails, etc., will work here.
Variations
You can mix and match the citrus. Use Seville orange juice, or lemons, or yuzu or whatever. Or use vinegar, or even verjus.
Ditto for the herb. Parsley, cilantro, culantro for a Cuban touch, pipicha, huacatay, summer savory, lovage, celery leaves, you name
it.
If you're not a butter fan, use a really good oil of your choice in its place, like a good olive oil, or an unrefined nut oil.

A vegetarian dish of fresh, unripened cheese cooked in a thick, creamy spinach purée, paneer palak originated in the northern Indian state
of Punjab. Named for its two primary ingredients — spinach and paneer cheese — palak paneer is reminiscent of saag paneer (which
typically uses a mixture of greens, including spinach, fenugreek leaves and mustard greens) but instead uses blended spinach as its sole
source of greens. A fresh, firm, mild cheese used throughout India, paneer is prized for its texture and its ability to absorb the flavors of its
surrounding ingredients, as it holds its shape without melting when heated. If youʼre unable to find paneer, you can try firm tofu instead.

This is a standard take on a beef rib roast, which is to say it is how my father made the dish when I was younger, and how I have mostly
made it since. The clear, rich fat that runs into the pan below the meat is the perfect vehicle for Yorkshire pudding.
INGREDIENTS PREPARATION

1 3-to-4-rib roast of beef, approximately 8 to 10
pounds Step 2
2 tablespoons unsalted butter Preheat oven to 450.
¼ cup all-purpose flour
2 tablespoons kosher salt Step 3
2 tablespoons freshly ground black pepper Rub butter on the cut ends of the roast.
Step 4
Combine flour, salt and pepper together in a small bowl, and then massage the mixture all
over the meat.
Step 5
Set the roast, rib side down, in a shallow roasting pan (the ribs act as a natural rack), and
place in the oven. Roast for approximately 20 to 30 minutes, or until the roast is nicely
darkened. Reduce oven to 350 and continue to roast, basting every 15 or 20 minutes, until
the roast reaches an internal temperature of 125 degrees (for medium-rare) on an instant-
read thermometer. Remove the roast to a cutting board and let rest for 20 minutes before
carving into either huge slabs or off the bone entirely and then thin slices.

# Red Beans and Rice Recipe

Every Monday, you can find a pot of red beans and rice cooking in someoneʼs kitchen in New Orleans. The food writer and New Orleans

## Recipe

Red Beans and Rice
Recipe from Pableaux Johnson
Adapted by Kim Severson
Total Time 2½ hours, plus at least 4 hoursʼ
soaking
Rating (4,072)
Every Monday, you can find a pot of red beans and rice cooking in someoneʼs kitchen in New Orleans. The food writer and New Orleans
bon vivant Pableaux Johnsonʼs house is no exception. The dish, an easy meal from when people used to reserve Monday to do the wash,
was once made with the pork bone left over from Sunday supper. In this version, Mr. Johnson strongly encourages the use of hand-made

# Roasted Cauliflower With Crispy Parmesan Recipe

The key to well-roasted cauliflower, with frizzled edges and sweet and tender middles, is to cook it at a high heat on a rack near the heat

## Overview
- **Total Time**: 45 minutes
- **Servings**: 4 servings Step 1

## Recipe

Roasted Cauliflower
With Crispy Parmesan
By Ali Slagle
Total Time 45 minutes
Rating (1,595)
The key to well-roasted cauliflower, with frizzled edges and sweet and tender middles, is to cook it at a high heat on a rack near the heat
source, mostly on one side. You could stop there or, toward the end of cooking, shower it with grated Parmesan to crisp and add a salty
boost. Follow the instructions in Step 1 to cut the cauliflower through the stem to create lots of flat sides, which yields more surface area for
browning and cheese — in other words, more of the good stuff.
INGREDIENTS PREPARATION
Yield: 4 servings Step 1
Arrange a rack at the bottom of the oven and heat to 450 degrees. With the stalk end facing
up, slice the cauliflower in half through the stalk, then when your knife reaches florets, pull
1 medium head cauliflower (about 2 pounds)
the pieces apart. (Pulling instead of cutting through the florets will prevent little buds from
3 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil
falling off.) Continue to slice through the stalks and pull apart florets until pieces are no
Salt and pepper thicker than 1 inch.
1½ ounces/¾ cup finely grated Parmesan
Step 2
On a sheet pan, toss the cauliflower pieces with the olive oil; season with salt and pepper.
Spread in an even layer, cut sides down. Roast, undisturbed, on the bottom rack until
golden brown on the underside, 15 to 20 minutes. (Check pieces in the middle of the pan,
because pieces at the edges brown faster.)
Step 3
Flip the cauliflower, sprinkle with the Parmesan, then roast until the cauliflower is tender
and the Parmesan is melted and golden in spots, 7 to 10 minutes. Let cool a few minutes for
the Parmesan to crisp. Use a spatula to transfer the cauliflower and any cheese on the
sheet pan to plates.

# Sesame Chicken Recipe

## Ingredients:

### For the Chicken:
- 1 lb (450g) boneless, skinless chicken thighs (or breasts), cut into bite-sized pieces
- 1/2 cup cornstarch (for coating)
- 1/4 cup all-purpose flour (optional for extra crispiness)
- 1 egg
- Salt and pepper to taste
- Oil for frying (vegetable or peanut oil)

### For the Sesame Sauce:
- 1/4 cup soy sauce
- 1/4 cup honey (or sugar for less sweetness)
- 2 tablespoons rice vinegar (or apple cider vinegar)
- 2 tablespoons ketchup (for color and tang)
- 1 tablespoon sesame oil
- 2 teaspoons cornstarch, dissolved in 2 tablespoons water (slurry for thickening)
- 1/2 cup water (or chicken broth for extra flavor)

### For Garnish:
- 1 tablespoon sesame seeds, toasted
- Chopped green onions (optional)

---

## Instructions:

### 1. Prepare the Chicken:
- In a bowl, lightly beat the egg, then season with a pinch of salt and pepper.
- Add the bite-sized chicken pieces into the egg mixture, making sure they are well coated.
- In a separate shallow bowl or plate, mix cornstarch and flour (if using). Coat the egg-covered chicken pieces with this mixture until evenly coated. Set aside.

### 2. Fry the Chicken:
- Heat oil in a deep skillet or frying pan over medium-high heat (about 350°F / 175°C).
- Fry the chicken pieces in batches, being careful not to overcrowd the pan. Cook for about 4-5 minutes per side, or until the chicken is golden brown and cooked through. 
- Remove the chicken from the oil and drain on paper towels.

### 3. Make the Sesame Sauce:
- In a small bowl, combine soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, ketchup, sesame oil, and water or chicken broth.
- Heat a large pan or wok over medium heat. Pour in the sauce mixture and bring it to a simmer.
- Stir in the cornstarch slurry to thicken the sauce. Cook for about 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, until the sauce becomes glossy and coats the back of a spoon.

### 4. Toss the Chicken:
- Add the fried chicken to the pan with the sauce. Toss everything together, making sure each piece is well coated with the sesame sauce.

### 5. Garnish and Serve:
- Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds and chopped green onions over the chicken.
- Serve hot with steamed rice and a side of vegetables (like broccoli or bok choy).

---

## Tips:
- **Crispier chicken**: Double-fry the chicken pieces by frying them a second time for an additional 1-2 minutes to make them extra crispy.
- **Spicy option**: Add 1-2 teaspoons of sriracha or red chili flakes to the sauce for a spicy kick.

# Sheet Pan Miso Salmon with Asparagus

## Overview

A one-pan weeknight dinner with miso-marinated salmon and roasted asparagus. The miso marinade penetrates deep for restaurant-quality flavor, and the broiler finish caramelizes the glaze perfectly. Minimal cleanup, maximum impact.

**Timeline:** 2-24 hours marinating + 20 minutes active cooking | **Yield:** 4 servings

---

## Ingredients

### For the Salmon

- 4 salmon fillets (6 oz each, skin-on or skinless)
- 1 lb asparagus, trimmed
- 2 tbsp neutral oil (divided)
- Salt and pepper

### Miso Marinade

- 3 tbsp white or yellow miso paste
- 2 tbsp mirin
- 1 tbsp sake (or dry white wine)
- 1 tbsp honey or brown sugar
- 1 tsp rice vinegar
- 1 tsp grated fresh ginger
- 1 clove garlic, minced

### Garnish

- Sesame seeds
- Sliced scallions
- Lemon wedges

---

## Instructions

### Step 1: Marinate Salmon (2-24 Hours Ahead)

1. **Make marinade:** Whisk together miso, mirin, sake, honey, vinegar, ginger, and garlic in bowl
2. **Reserve marinade:** Set aside 2 tbsp marinade in separate container for finishing (refrigerate)
3. **Marinate salmon:** Coat salmon fillets flesh-side with remaining marinade
4. **Refrigerate:** Cover and refrigerate 2-24 hours
    - Minimum 2 hours: good flavor
    - Overnight (12-24 hours): restaurant-level depth
    - Don't exceed 24 hours: miso can over-cure

### Step 2: Prep Sheet Pan

1. **Preheat oven** to 400°F (200°C)
2. **Line sheet pan** with parchment paper
3. **Prep salmon:** Remove from fridge, wipe off excess marinade with paper towel (leave thin coating)
    - Critical: excess marinade burns during cooking

### Step 3: Arrange on Sheet Pan

1. **Prep asparagus:** Toss with 1 tbsp oil, salt, and pepper
2. **Arrange asparagus:** Spread in single layer on outer edges of pan
3. **Place salmon:** Position fillets in center, skin-side down (if skin-on)
4. **Oil salmon:** Drizzle with remaining 1 tbsp oil

### Step 4: Bake (12-15 Min)

1. **Bake** at 400°F for 10-12 minutes
2. **Check doneness:**
    - Salmon internal temp ~135°F
    - Asparagus tender-crisp
    - Salmon should be almost cooked through but not quite done

### Step 5: Broiler Finish (2-3 Min)

1. **Switch to broil:** Set oven to high broil
2. **Glaze salmon:** Brush with reserved marinade
3. **Broil** 2-3 minutes until miso caramelizes and bubbles
4. **Watch closely:** Miso can burn fast
5. **Final temp:** Salmon should reach 145°F internal

### Step 6: Serve

1. **Garnish:** Sprinkle with sesame seeds and sliced scallions
2. **Serve:** With lemon wedges on the side

---

## Why This Works

- **Miso marinade penetrates deep:** Enzymes tenderize and flavor the fish from within
- **Single pan:** Everything cooks together, minimal cleanup
- **Timing alignment:** Asparagus and salmon finish simultaneously at 400°F
- **Broiler finish:** Caramelizes miso glaze without overcooking fish
- **No flipping needed:** Set it and forget it until broiler step

---

## Tips & Variations

### Sheet Pan Success

- **Don't overcrowd:** Asparagus needs space to roast, not steam
- **Asparagus thickness:**
    - Thin spears: 10-12 min
    - Thick spears: 12-15 min (adjust timing)
- **Parchment vs foil:** Parchment prevents sticking without muting the roast

### Salmon Doneness

- **Visual check:** Flakes easily, opaque throughout
- **Temp check:** 145°F internal (FDA recommendation)
- **Preference:** 135°F for medium-rare (moister, less firm)

### Variations

**Different vegetables:**
- Broccoli florets
- Brussels sprouts (halved)
- Snap peas
- Bok choy (add last 5 minutes)

**Add starch to the pan:**
- Halved baby potatoes (toss with oil, add 10 min before salmon)
- Cubed sweet potato (par-cook 10 min, then add salmon)

**Different fish:**
- Black cod (traditional with miso)
- Arctic char
- Trout fillets

---

## Serving Suggestions

**Pair with:**
- Steamed rice or quinoa (cook separately)
- Simple cucumber salad
- Miso soup

**Leftovers:**
- Flake salmon over rice bowls
- Add to grain salads
- Use in nori wraps

---

## Timeline

**Day Before (or morning of):**
- 5 min: Make marinade, coat salmon, refrigerate

**Day Of:**
- 5 min: Prep sheet pan, arrange asparagus and salmon
- 12 min: Bake
- 3 min: Broiler finish
- **Total active time:** 20 minutes

---

## Baker's Notes

This recipe is a weeknight workhorse. The marinade does the heavy lifting - your only job is not to overcook the fish. The longer marinate (overnight) makes this taste like a $40 restaurant dish. Batch the marinade on Sunday, marinate 4 fillets, and you have an elegant dinner ready to bake any night of the week.

Works beautifully for Sarah's meal plan (healthy fats, protein, omega-3s, skin-glowing ingredients). Nick can enjoy it on his gut-healing protocol days when salmon is featured.

# Shepherds_Pie_Recipe

## Overview
- **Servings**: 4

## Ingredients
**For the meat filling:**
- 1 tablespoon olive oil
- 1 medium onion, diced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 medium carrot, diced
- 1 rib celery, diced
- 1 lb ground lamb or beef
- 1 tablespoon tomato paste
- 1 cup beef broth
- 1 teaspoon Worcestershire sauce
- 1/2 teaspoon dried thyme
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
- 1/2 cup frozen peas
- 1/2 cup frozen corn

**For the mashed potato topping:**
- 1 1/2 lbs potatoes, peeled and cubed
- 1/4 cup milk
- 2 tablespoons butter
- Salt and pepper to taste

## Instructions
1. Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
2. Cook the potatoes: In a pot of salted water, boil potatoes until fork-tender (about 15 minutes).
3. Drain. Mash with milk, butter, salt, and pepper until smooth. Set aside.
3. Prepare the meat filling: In a skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat. Sauté onion, garlic, carrot,
4. and celery for about 5 minutes. Add ground lamb or beef and cook until browned. Stir in tomato
5. paste, Worcestershire sauce, broth, thyme, salt, and pepper. Simmer 10 minutes. Stir in peas and
6. corn.
4. Assemble the pie: Spread the meat mixture evenly in a baking dish. Spoon mashed potatoes on
5. top and smooth them out. Use a fork to create ridges on the surface (helps it brown).
5. Bake: Bake for 20-25 minutes or until the top is golden brown. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.

# Silky_Truffle_Parmesan_Cream_Sauce

Silky Truffle Parmesan Cream Sauce

## Ingredients
- 2 tbsp unsalted butter
- 2 cloves garlic, smashed (not minced)
- 1 cup heavy cream
- ¾ cup finely grated Parmigiano-Reggiano
- 1-2 tsp truffle carpaccio + 1 tsp truffle oil (from jar)
- Salt and black pepper to taste
- Optional: white pepper or nutmeg

## Instructions
1. Infuse Cream with Truffle & Garlic:
2. * In a saucepan, gently melt butter over medium-low heat.
3. * Add smashed garlic cloves and chopped truffle carpaccio.
4. * Add the cream and let it heat gently for 5-8 minutes (do not boil).
5. * Stir in 1 tsp truffle oil if desired.
2. Strain:
3. * Strain cream through a fine mesh strainer into a clean saucepan.
4. * Discard solids or reserve for another use.
3. Add Cheese Smoothly:
4. * On low heat, whisk in grated Parmesan until fully melted and smooth.
5. * Season with salt, pepper, and optional nutmeg.
4. Toss and Serve:
5. * Toss with pasta and serve immediately. Garnish with extra shaved Parmesan if desired.
6. Optional Ultra-Smooth Variation:
7. * Blend the infused cream (with truffle and garlic) before adding cheese for a speckled but chunk-free sauce.

## Instructions
1. Combine all of the ingredients for the brine in a large pot and bring to a boil. Let cool. If
2. you're short on time, you can also start by boiling the brine with just 2 quarts of water and
3. then adding 64 ounces of ice to quickly cool down to 1 gallon of brine.
4. Smoked Turkey Legs (Disney Copycat Recipe) - The Woks of Life
2. While that's happening, rinse your turkey legs and set aside in a large container (one that will
3. fit into your refrigerator). You may want to use two separate containers. When the brine has
4. cooled, pour the brine over the turkey legs, making sure they are totally submerged. Cover
5. and refrigerate for 24 hours. (If you want to expedite the process or simply have very large
6. turkey legs, use a marinade injector. Inject 2-5 syringes-full of brine into each turkey leg. If
7. expediting, brine the injected turkey legs for 5-6 hours rather than the full 24 hours. If you're
8. just using larger legs and want to make sure they're flavorful, you can brine for the full 24
9. hours after injecting.)
3. When the turkey legs are ready, heat your charcoal. Your key tools for this recipe are a
4. charcoal grill, a chimney starter, charcoal, and wet wood chips, which provides the smoky
5. flavor. Fill your chimney with charcoal and light the coals with a piece of newspaper. Let heat
6. for a solid 15-20 minutes or so, until the coals are slightly white hot. Also, take 1-2 handfuls of
7. wood chips and soak them in water while the coals are heating.
4. At this point, if you haven't already injected your turkey legs with brine, you can do so,
5. injecting them with 4-5 syringes full of brine at various points around each leg, to ensure
6. they're moist and juicy before cooking.
5. Pour the coals into the grill and scatter the wood chips around the coals. Lay your grill rack
6. over the coals. Place the turkey legs on the grill rack and close the grill.
6. 1 chimney-full of coal is enough to start for an average-sized charcoal grill. Add another
7. chimney of coal every 20-30 minutes, depending on the kind of charcoal you're using.
8. Periodically add additional wet wood chips to make more smoke as needed. More wood chips
9. makes more smoke, increasing the "hammy" smoked flavor of the turkey legs. You can cater
10. this to your personal preferences. I like a very hammy smoked turkey leg; my aunt prefers
11. more of a natural flavor. Take your pick!
7. The slow cooking method is key here. Periodically check the turkey legs, turning every once in
8. a while, and make sure the grill maintains a temperature of 300-325°F (150-160°C). There is
9. some element of trial and error to this if you're a first-timer; make observations and adjust
10. amounts of charcoal, wood chips, and heat over the course of the cooking time.
8. Maintain the grill, charcoal, and wood chips, letting the turkey cook for 3½ to 4 hours, until
9. the turkey legs have a nice, dark smoky color.

# Smoked Turkey Recipe

There are countless advantages to smoke-roasting (also known barbecuing) your turkey, as in this recipe from the barbecue expert Steven

## Overview
- **Servings**: 10 to 12 servings Step 1

## Recipe

Smoked Turkey
By Steven Raichlen
Total Time About 3 hours, plus brining
Rating (246)
There are countless advantages to smoke-roasting (also known barbecuing) your turkey, as in this recipe from the barbecue expert Steven
Raichlen. Smoking produces a bird of incomparable succulence, especially when combined with another traditional American barbecue
technique, brining. There is the rich, evocative flavor of wood smoke, and the burnished mahogany sheen it gives the bird. Then there's the
simplicity of the method: once you put the bird in the smoker or on the grill, you pretty much leave it there until it is done, while the kitchen
and oven are freed up for side dishes and desserts. Last but certainly not least, you get an excuse to spend a fall afternoon outdoors, maybe
with beer in hand.
INGREDIENTS PREPARATION
Yield: 10 to 12 servings Step 1
Set up an outdoor grill for indirect grilling, placing a large foil drip pan in center. (If using
a smoker, light and set it up according to manufacturer's instructions and heat to 275
1 10- to 12-pound turkey, brined (see recipe)
degrees. In a smoker, you will need to cook bird longer, 3½ to 4½ hours.)
2 tablespoons melted unsalted butter
Step 2
Drain bird. Blot dry inside and out and truss if desired. Place in center of grill grate, over
drip pan and between mounds of natural lump charcoal. Toss ½ cup of soaked wood chops
on each mound of coals. Place lid on grill. Adjust vents to keep temperature between 325
and 350 degrees.
Step 3
Grill turkey until darkly browned and cooked through, 2½ to 3 hours. Baste turkey with
melted butter after first hour and every hour thereafter. If skin starts to brown too much,
loosely tent bird with foil. Use an instant-read thermometer to test for doneness; turkey is
ready when internal temperature of the thigh is 180 degrees. Replenish charcoal every
hour, adding 8 to 10 lumps of charcoal to each mound of coals and leaving grill uncovered
for a few minutes to allow charcoal to light. After 1 hour, add 1½ cups of soaked wood
chips.
Step 4
Transfer turkey to a platter, loosely tent with foil, and let rest for 10 minutes before
carving. Reserve any drippings in drip pan for gravy.

# Spicy Carrot-Ginger Soup

## Description
A bright, well-balanced soup featuring carrots stewed with ginger and jalapeño, finished with lime and cilantro. Unlike typical thick purées, this soup has a lighter consistency. The soup can be made ahead and reheated just before serving for the freshest taste.

## Ingredients
### For the Soup
- 4 tablespoons unsalted butter
- 1 large yellow or white onion, sliced (about 1½ cups)
- 6 garlic cloves
- 2 pounds carrots, preferably young, peeled and sliced ¼ inch thick
- 1 jalapeño, stemmed, seeded and sliced
- 1 (2-inch) chunk of ginger, peeled and thinly sliced
- 6 cups chicken or vegetable broth, plus more as needed
- Salt and pepper
- 1 tablespoon lime juice
- 1 teaspoon lime zest
- 1 small bunch cilantro

### For the Ginger-Chive Cream
- ½ cup crème fraîche or sour cream
- 1 teaspoon finely grated fresh ginger
- 1 tablespoon very finely sliced chives
- Salt to taste

## Instructions
1. Melt butter in Dutch oven over medium heat. Add onion and garlic with salt and pepper. Cook until softened (about 10 minutes), avoiding browning.

2. Add carrots, jalapeño, and sliced ginger. Stir to coat with salt. Add broth, bring to boil, then simmer until carrots are tender (10-15 minutes).

3. Let soup cool to room temperature if possible.

4. Meanwhile, make ginger-chive cream by combining crème fraîche, grated ginger, chives, and salt.

5. Purée cooled soup in blender until smooth. Adjust salt and add broth to achieve heavy cream consistency.

6. To serve:
   - Reheat soup over low heat
   - Stir in lime juice, zest, and chopped cilantro
   - Ladle into bowls
   - Top with ginger-chive cream and cilantro sprigs

## Yield
4 to 6 servings

## Time
- Total: 55 minutes
- Prep: 15 minutes
- Cook: 40 minutes

## Notes
- Can be made with butternut or kabocha squash instead of carrots
- Cool soup before adding cilantro to maintain freshness
- An immersion blender can be used instead of a regular blender
- Additional broth may be needed to achieve desired consistency
- Soup should be the consistency of heavy cream, not thick or stodgy
- Taste and adjust salt throughout cooking process to enhance flavors
- Consider grating the sliced ginger for better blending

1. Before You Start: Prepare your sushi rice ahead of time. For instructions, see my step-by-step guide
2. on How to Make Sushi Rice. For this recipe, you‘ll need 1½ cups sushi rice (cooked and seasoned) as
3. each roll requires ¾ US cup (110 g) of sushi rice. ¾ cup uncooked Japanese short-grain rice is 1 rice
4. cooker cup (150 g, 5.3 oz), which yields roughly 2¼ cups (330 g) of cooked rice. Important: Cover the
5. sushi rice with a damp cloth at all times to prevent it from drying.
6. Spicy Tuna Roll - Just One Cookbook
2. Gather all the ingredients.
3. Make the vinegared water for dipping your fingers (tezu) by combining ¼ cup water and 2 tsp rice
4. vinegar (unseasoned) in a small bowl. Tip: Dipping your fingers prevents rice from sticking to them.
4. Cut 4 oz sashimi-grade tuna into ¼-inch (0.5-cm) cubes; alternatively, you can mince the tuna.
5. In a medium bowl, combine the tuna, 3 tsp sriracha sauce, ½ tsp toasted sesame oil, and most of the
6. sliced 2 green onions/scallions (set aside some for topping each roll).
7. Spicy Tuna Roll - Just One Cookbook
8. To Roll the Sushi
1. Cut your 1 sheet nori (dried laver seaweed) in half crosswise. Lay a half nori sheet, shiny side down,
2. on a bamboo sushi mat covered with a layer of plastic film. Wet your fingers in the tezu and spread ¾ cup
3. (110 g) sushi rice evenly onto the nori sheet. Sprinkle the rice with 1 Tbsp of the total 2 Tbsp toasted
4. white sesame seeds called for in this recipe.
2. Turn the sheet of nori over so that the rice side is facing down against the plastic wrap. Line the edge of the
3. nori sheet at the bottom end of the bamboo mat. Place half of the tuna mixture (if you‘re making 2
4. rolls) in a thin row along the bottom end of the nori sheet.
3. Grab the bottom edge of the bamboo mat while keeping the fillings in place with your fingers and roll into a
4. tight cylinder. Lift the edge of the bamboo mat and continue to roll it forward while keeping gentle pressure
5. on the mat. Repeat with the rest of the ingredients.
6. To Serve
1. With a very sharp knife, cut the Spicy Tuna Roll in half and then cut each half into 3 pieces. Clean the knife
2. with a damp cloth every few cuts. When you cut sushi rolls, dip your fingers in tezu or cover the roll with
3. Spicy Tuna Roll - Just One Cookbook
4. plastic, so the rice won‘t stick to your hands.
2. Put a dollop of Homemade Spicy Mayo on top of each sushi piece and garnish with the remaining green
3. onion.
4. To Store
1. It‘s best to enjoy sushi rolls on the same day. Rice gets hard and dry in the refrigerator. Therefore, if you
2. really want to keep sushi rolls in the refrigerator, my recommendation is to cover them with plastic and a

# Stromboli - Sally_s Baking Addiction

How to Make Homemade Stromboli - Sally's Baking Addiction

## Overview
- **Prep Time**: 2 hours Cook Time
- **Cook Time**: 25 minutes
- **Total Time**: 2 hours

## Ingredients
- Homemade Dough for 2
- 1 and 1/3 cups (320ml) warm water (between 100-110°F, 38-43°C)
- 2 and 1/4 teaspoons (7g) instant or active-dry yeast (1 standard packet)
- 1 Tablespoon (13g) granulated sugar
- 2 Tablespoons (30ml) olive oil
- 1 teaspoon salt
- 3 and 1/2 cups (about 450g) all-purpose flour (spooned & leveled), plus more for
- hands and work surface

**Fillings for 2**
- 3 Tablespoons (43g) unsalted butter, melted
- 2 garlic cloves, minced (or 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder)
- 2 teaspoons chopped fresh parsley (or 1 teaspoon dried)
- 1 pound thinly sliced meats such as Italian cold cuts, deli ham, or large pepperoni
- slices*
- 3/4 – 1 pound cheese (about 3 cups shredded or about 16-20 slices deli cheese)*
- Egg Wash & Topping for 2
- egg wash: 1 large egg beaten with 1 Tablespoon water
- optional: sprinkle of chopped fresh or dried parsley, coarse sea salt or flaky sea salt,
- pepper, Italian seasoning, and/or parmesan cheese
- Cook Mode Prevent your screen from going dark

## Instructions
1. How to Make Homemade Stromboli - Sally's Baking Addiction
2. 1 Whisk the warm water, yeast, and granulated sugar together in the bowl of your stand mixer
3. fitted with a dough hook or paddle attachment. Cover and allow to rest for 5 minutes. *If
4. you don’t have a stand mixer, simply use a large mixing bowl and mix the dough with a
5. wooden spoon or silicone spatula in the next step.
6. 2 Add the olive oil, salt, and flour. Beat on low speed for 2 minutes.
7. 3 Knead the dough: Keep the dough in the mixer (and switch to the dough hook if using the
8. paddle) and beat for an additional 5 full minutes, or knead by hand on a lightly floured
9. surface for 5 full minutes. (If you’re new to bread-baking, my How to Knead Dough video
10. tutorial can help here.) If the dough becomes too sticky during the kneading process,
11. sprinkle 1 teaspoon of flour at a time on the dough or on the work surface/in the bowl to
12. make a soft, slightly tacky dough. Do not add more flour than you need because you do not
13. want a dry dough. After kneading, the dough should still feel a little soft. Poke it with your
14. finger—if it slowly bounces back, your dough is ready to rise. You can also do a
15. “windowpane test” to see if your dough has been kneaded long enough: tear off a small
16. (roughly golfball-size) piece of dough and gently stretch it out until it’s thin enough for light
17. to pass through it. Hold it up to a window or light. Does light pass through the stretched
18. dough without the dough tearing first? If so, your dough has been kneaded long enough
19. and is ready to rise. If not, keep kneading until it passes the windowpane test.
20. 4 Rise: Lightly grease a large bowl with oil or nonstick spray—just use the same bowl you
21. used for the dough. Place the dough in the bowl, turning it to coat all sides in the oil. Cover
22. the bowl with aluminum foil, plastic wrap, or a clean kitchen towel. Allow the dough to rise
23. at room temperature for 60-90 minutes or until double in size. If using instant yeast, this
24. takes about 1 hour. (Tip: For the warm environment on a particularly cold day, heat your
25. oven to 150°F (66°C). Turn the oven off, place the dough inside, and keep the door slightly
26. ajar. This will be a warm environment for your dough to rise. After about 30 minutes, close
27. the oven door to trap the air inside with the rising dough. When it’s doubled in size, remove
28. from the oven.)
29. 5 Preheat oven to 400°F (204°). Line 2 large baking sheets with parchment paper or silicone
30. baking mats.
31. 6 Shape the dough: When the dough is ready, punch it down to release the air. Divide in half.
32. (If you aren’t making 2 strombolis, freeze the other half of dough. See freezing instructions
33. below.) On a lightly floured work surface using a lightly floured rolling pin, roll each half of
34. dough into a 10×16-inch rectangle. I like to use my hands to square off the edges, as shown
35. in the video below. If the dough keeps shrinking as you try to shape it, cover it lightly and
36. let the dough rest for 10 minutes before trying again. (The gluten just needs to settle.)
37. 7 Add fillings: Mix melted butter and garlic together. Spread all over each rectangle. Sprinkle
38. each with parsley. When you start layering on meats and cheeses, leave a 1 inch border on
39. the bottom and sides and a 3 inch border on top. (Basically you’ll have an empty 3×16-inch
40. gap on top that only has butter/garlic on it. This is because when rolling, the fillings will be
41. pushed forward. See photos and video below if you need a visual.) Arrange a layer sliced
42. meats onto each dough, usually about 8-10 slices on each depending on size and thickness
43. of slices. Add a layer of cheese. Repeat with more meat and cheese until all is used—about
44. How to Make Homemade Stromboli - Sally's Baking Addiction
45. 1/2 pound meat and 1/2 pound cheese per stromboli. Brush all edges with egg wash,
46. including 3 inch gap at the top. This helps the stromboli hold its rolled shape. Slowly roll
47. each into a tight 16 inch log, folding in the two ends as you roll. See me do this in the video
48. below. Dust your hands or the dough with flour if things become too sticky. Carefully
49. transfer each to lined baking sheets. Pinch or tuck in ends to seal if they became unfolded.
50. 8 Brush each stromboli with egg wash and, if desired, optional toppings. Using a very sharp
51. knife, cut 3-4 slits into the tops of each, which helps steam escape. At this point, you can
52. cover shaped stromboli tightly and refrigerate for up to 8 hours.
53. 9 Bake for about 25 minutes or until crust is golden brown—if you have an instant read
54. thermometer, the center of the stromboli should be at least 200ºF (93ºC). If meats are
55. particularly greasy (like pepperoni), some grease will spill out the sides. Cheese may bubble
56. out the sides or top slits, too. If baking both at the same time, rotate pans halfway through
57. baking and extend bake time (if needed) by 2-3 minutes. Remove from the oven and cool
58. on baking sheets for 5 minutes before transferring to a cutting board and slicing.
59. 10 Serve plain or with pizza/marinara sauce for dipping.
60. 11 Cover and store leftover stromboli (slices or whole) in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.

## Ingredients
- 1 12-14 pound whole packer brisket

- 2 Tablespoons coarse ground black pepper

## Instructions
1. Store your brisket in the refrigerator until you are ready to start trimming. Cold briskets are much
2. easier to work with. Flip your brisket over so the point end is underneath. Remove any silver skin
3. or excess fat from the flat muscle. Trim down the large crescent moon shaped fat section until it is
4. a smooth transition between the point and the flat. Trim and excessive or loose meat and fat from
5. the point. Square the edges and ends of the flat. Flip the brisket over and trim the top fat cap to
6. about 1/4 of an inch thickness across the surface of the brisket.
2. In a mixing bowl or empty spice container, mix the salt, pepper, and garlic. Share over the brisket
3. to evenly distribute the spices on all sides.
3. Preheat your smoker to 225 degrees F using indirect heat and hardwood smoke. Place the brisket
4. on the smoker with the point end facing your main heat source. This is a thicker part of the
5. brisket and it can handle the additional heat. Close the lid and smoke until and internal
6. thermometer reads 165 degrees F (usually takes around 8 hours).
4. On a large work surface, roll out a big piece of butcher paper (or foil) and center your brisket in
5. the middle. Wrap the brisket by folding edge over edge, creating a leak proof seal all the way
6. around. Return the wrapped brisket to the smoker, seam side down so the weight from the
7. brisket crimps the edges of the paper wrap down tight.
5. Close the lid on the smoker and, maintaining 225 degrees F, continue cooking until the internal
6. temperature of the brisket reaches 202 degrees F in the thickest part of the meat (takes anywhere
7. from 5-8 hours).
6. Remove the brisket to a large cutting board and allow to rest for 1 hour before slicing. Slice both
7. the point and the flat against the grain with a sharp knife and serve immediately.
