content:
# The Best Pizza Dough Recipe

The Best Pizza Dough Recipe - Sugar Spun Run

## Overview
- **Prep Time**: 15 minutes
- **Cook Time**: 15 minutes
- **Total Time**: 1 hour
- **Servings**: 12 servings

## Ingredients
- 2-2 ⅓ cups all-purpose flour OR bread flour¹ divided (250-295g)
- 1 packet instant yeast² (2 ¼ teaspoon)
- 1 ½ teaspoons sugar
- ¾ teaspoon salt
- ⅛-¼ teaspoon garlic powder and/or dried basil leaves optional
- 2 Tablespoons olive oil + additional
- ¾ cup warm water³ (175ml)

## Instructions
1. Combine 1 cup (125g) of flour, instant yeast, sugar, and salt in a large bowl. If desired, add
2. garlic powder and dried basil at this point as well.
2. Add olive oil and warm water and use a wooden spoon to stir well very well.
3. Gradually add another 1 cup (125g) of flour. Add any additional flour as needed (I've found
4. that sometimes I need as much as an additional ⅓ cup), stirring until the dough is forming
5. into a cohesive, elastic ball and is beginning to pull away from the sides of the bowl (see video
6. above recipe for visual cue). The dough will still be slightly sticky but still should be
7. manageable with your hands.
4. Drizzle a separate, large, clean bowl generously with olive oil and use a pastry brush to brush
5. up the sides of the bowl.
5. Lightly dust your hands with flour and form your pizza dough into a round ball and transfer to
6. your olive oil-brushed bowl. Use your hands to roll the pizza dough along the inside of the
7. bowl until it is coated in olive oil, then cover the bowl tightly with plastic wrap and place it in a
8. warm place.
6. Allow dough to rise for 30 minutes or until doubled in size. If you intend to bake this dough
7. into a pizza, I also recommend preheating your oven to 425F (215C) at this point so that it will
8. have reached temperature once your pizza is ready to bake.
7. Once the dough has risen, use your hands to gently deflate it and transfer to a lightly floured
8. surface and knead briefly until smooth (about 3-5 times).
9. The Best Pizza Dough Recipe - Sugar Spun Run
8. Use either your hands or a rolling pin to work the dough into 12" circle.
9. Transfer dough to a parchment paper lined pizza pan and either pinch the edges or fold them
10. over to form a crust.
10. Drizzle additional olive oil (about a Tablespoon) over the top of the pizza and use your pastry
11. brush to brush the entire surface of the pizza (including the crust) with olive oil.
11. Use a fork to poke holes all over the center of the pizza to keep the dough from bubbling up
12. in the oven.
12. Add desired toppings (see the notes for a link to my favorite, 5-minute pizza sauce recipe!)
13. and bake in a 425F (215C) preheated oven for 13-15 minutes or until toppings are golden
14. brown. Slice and serve.

## Notes
¹I've found that all-purpose flour yields a softer crust while bread flour gives a slightly crispier
exterior. Please see the post for more information on all-purpose vs. bread flour in pizza dough.
²Many commenters have reported using active dry yeast (use the same amount, 2 ¼ teaspoon)
with success. Some people have proofed the yeast first with the ¾ cup warm water, which is what I
would recommend, while others have just mixed it into the dough as instructed. Both have had
success!
³Ideally your water should be between 105-115F (40-46C). I usually just use warm tap water but do
make sure that your water isn't too hot or it will kill your yeast!
Making in Advance:
To make in advance, let the dough rise covered at room temperature as indicated in the recipe,
then deflate it, wrap it tightly so it doesn't dry out, and store in the refrigerator for up to several
days or it will freeze for up to a month.
Top your pizza off with my favorite, easy, homemade pizza sauce!

# Three Sisters Stew

## Description
This recipe for Three Sisters Stew is adapted from Pamela Sinclair's cookbook "A Taste of Wyoming". It honors the agricultural tradition of Plains Indians, featuring the trinity of corn, beans, and squash. This hearty stew works well as a rich side dish for turkey or as a main course.

## Ingredients
- 1 pound trimmed pork loin, cut into 1-inch cubes
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- Kosher salt and black pepper, as needed
- 2 tablespoons neutral oil (e.g., canola)
- 1 large yellow onion, diced
- 3 garlic cloves, minced
- 4 cups turkey or chicken stock
- 1 medium yellow squash, diced
- 1 (15-ounce) can pinto beans, drained
- 1 (15-ounce) can black beans, drained
- 1 (14½-ounce) can chopped tomatoes
- 2 cups fresh or frozen corn kernels
- 1 (4-ounce) can roasted green chiles (½ cup)
- ½ bunch fresh cilantro, roughly chopped

## Instructions
1. Season pork with cumin, salt, and pepper. Heat oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown pork in batches, about 5-6 minutes. Set aside.

2. In the same pan, sauté onion until translucent (5-7 minutes). Add garlic and sauté for 2-3 minutes.

3. Return pork to pan with stock and squash. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for about 30 minutes.

4. Add beans, tomatoes, corn, and chiles. Cook uncovered over medium heat until stew has thickened, about 40 minutes.

5. Stir in cilantro and season to taste with salt and pepper.

## Yield
8 servings

## Time
Total time: 1 hour 40 minutes

## Notes
- For a vegetarian version, omit the pork and add 1 pound of cubed butternut squash instead.
- Some cooks suggest using butternut squash in place of yellow squash for a more authentic "three sisters" combination.
- The stew can be made in a slow cooker: brown the meat and vegetables, then cook on low for 6 hours.
- Adding wild rice or a brown rice/wild rice combo can make the stew thicker and more hearty.
- For more heat, consider adding extra chiles or red pepper flakes.
- The stew can be made with turkey or chicken instead of pork.

# Tomato-Ginger Chicken and Rice Soup

## Description
This soup is a gentle yet subtly spicy dish, reminiscent of sizzling rice soup and tom yum. It features a caramelized base of tomato paste and fried ginger, with fresh tomatoes added for brightness. The soup can be adjusted to be calming and mild or more robust and pungent.

## Ingredients

- 1/4 cup tomato paste

- Salt and pepper
- 6 cups (1 1/2 quarts) chicken broth
- 1 to 1 1/2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs
- 3/4 cup long-grain white rice (unrinsed)
- 1 pint (about 10 ounces) cherry or other small tomatoes
- 2 tablespoons fish sauce or soy sauce, plus more to taste
- 1 lime, cut into wedges, for squeezing
- Toasted sesame oil or chile oil, for serving (optional)

## Instructions
1. In a large pot, heat the butter over medium. Add tomato paste and ginger, season with salt and pepper, and cook until tomato paste darkens, 2 to 4 minutes.

2. Add broth, chicken thighs, and rice. Season lightly with salt. Bring to a simmer and cook for 15 minutes.

3. Roughly quarter the tomatoes. Add to the soup and simmer until chicken is cooked and rice starts to break down, 10 to 15 minutes more.

4. Remove chicken, shred it, and return to the pot. Stir in fish sauce.

5. Season to taste with additional fish sauce and pepper.

6. Serve with a squeeze of lime juice and a few drops of sesame or chile oil, if using.

## Yield
4 servings

## Time
- Total Time: 55 minutes
- Prep Time: 5 minutes
- Cook Time: 50 minutes

## Notes
- For a milder soup, use less fish sauce and lime. For a more powerful soup, add more.
- The rice is meant to break down and lose its shape, creating a thicker consistency.
- Some cooks prefer to cook and add the rice separately to maintain its texture.
- Adding juice from half a lime to the entire pot at the end can enhance the flavors.
- Consider adding avocado chunks, baby spinach, or cilantro as additional toppings.
- For extra heat, you can add crushed red pepper or a small amount of scotch bonnet pepper.

title: Traditional Sourdough Bread
description: This classic sourdough recipe produces a beautifully tangy loaf with an open, chewy crumb and crispy crust. Using only flour, water, salt, and your active starter, this is bread-making at its most fundamental and rewarding.
ingredients: 100g active sourdough starter (100% hydration, fed and bubbly)
content:
# Traditional Sourdough Bread

## Overview

This classic sourdough recipe produces a beautifully tangy loaf with an open, chewy crumb and crispy crust. Using only flour, water, salt, and your active starter, this is bread-making at its most fundamental and rewarding.

**Timeline:** 2 days total | **Yield:** 1 large boule or 2 smaller loaves

---

## Ingredients

### For the Bread

- 100g active sourdough starter (100% hydration, fed and bubbly)
- 375g lukewarm water
- 500g bread flour
- 10g salt

### Starter Preparation (Night Before)

- Your existing starter
- 50g bread flour
- 50g water

---

## Day 1: Feed Starter & Mix Dough

### Evening (6-8 PM): Feed Your Starter

1. **Refresh starter:** Take 20g of your existing starter, add 50g flour and 50g water
2. Mix well, cover loosely, leave at room temperature overnight
3. Starter should double in size and be very bubbly by morning (8-12 hours)

### Morning (8-10 AM): Float Test & Mix Dough

1. **Test starter readiness:** Drop a spoonful in water - it should float
2. **Autolyse:** Mix flour and water only, let rest 30 minutes
3. **Add starter:** Combine 100g active starter with the flour-water mixture
4. **Add salt:** Sprinkle salt over dough, mix until well incorporated
5. **Initial mix:** Combine until no dry flour remains (dough will be shaggy)

### Bulk Fermentation (4-6 Hours)

**Coil Folds Schedule:**

- **30 minutes after mixing:** First fold
- **1 hour later:** Second fold
- **1 hour later:** Third fold
- **1 hour later:** Fourth fold
- **Rest:** Let rise undisturbed for remaining time

**Fold Technique:**

1. Wet hands to prevent sticking
2. Grab one side of dough, stretch up and fold over to opposite side
3. Rotate bowl 90° and repeat 3 more times
4. Cover and rest

**Signs Bulk is Complete:**

- Dough increased by 50-70% in size
- Jiggly and airy when gently shaken
- Visible bubbles on surface
- Poke test: slow spring-back

---

## Day 1 Evening: Pre-Shape & Shape

### Pre-Shape (5-7 PM)

1. **Turn out dough** onto lightly floured surface
2. **Pre-shape** into rough round using bench scraper
3. **Rest** 20-30 minutes until relaxed

### Final Shape

1. **Shape into boule:**
    
    - Flip dough seam-side up
    - Fold top edge down to center
    - Fold left and right edges to center
    - Roll tightly from top to bottom
    - Create tension by dragging on counter
2. **Final proof setup:**
    
    - Place seam-side up in banneton or bowl lined with floured towel
    - Cover with damp towel or plastic
    - Refrigerate overnight (12-48 hours)

---

## Day 2: Bake

### Morning: Prepare to Bake

1. **Preheat:** Dutch oven at 500°F (260°C) for 45 minutes
2. **Score:** Turn dough onto parchment, score with sharp blade
    - One deep slash or decorative pattern
    - Cut quickly and confidently

### Baking Process

1. **Initial bake:** Lower into Dutch oven on parchment, cover
    
    - Bake 20 minutes at 500°F
2. **Finish bake:** Remove lid, reduce to 450°F (230°C)
    
    - Bake 20-25 minutes until deep golden brown
    - Internal temperature should reach 205-210°F
3. **Cool:** Transfer to wire rack
    
    - Cool completely before slicing (2+ hours minimum)
    - Crust will crisp as it cools

---

## Traditional Techniques

### Starter Maintenance

- **Feeding ratio:** 1:1:1 (starter:flour:water) for maintenance
- **Peak activity:** Use when doubled and just starting to fall
- **Storage:** Refrigerate if not baking daily

### Dough Assessment

- **Windowpane test:** Stretch small piece - should be translucent without tearing
- **Poke test:** Gently poke shaped dough - slow spring-back indicates readiness
- **Visual cues:** Look for 50-70% size increase during bulk fermentation

### Environmental Factors

- **Temperature:** Warmer = faster fermentation (ideal: 75-78°F)
- **Humidity:** Cover dough to prevent skin formation
- **Timing:** Adjust schedule based on your starter's activity level

---

## Troubleshooting

### Common Issues

**Dense, heavy loaf:**

- Starter wasn't active enough
- Under-fermented (bulk too short)
- Over-proofed (final proof too long)

**Flat, spreading loaf:**

- Insufficient gluten development
- Over-hydrated dough
- Poor shaping technique

**Lack of sourness:**

- Younger starter (develops more tang with age)
- Shorter fermentation time
- Try longer cold proof (up to 48 hours)

### Success Indicators

**Good dough:**

- Smooth, slightly tacky surface after folds
- Holds shape when formed
- Passes windowpane test

**Proper fermentation:**

- Visible bubbles throughout
- Jiggly when gently shaken
- 50-70% size increase

**Perfect bake:**

- Deep golden crust
- Hollow sound when tapped
- Internal temp 205-210°F

---

## Variations

### Whole Grain Version

- Replace 100g bread flour with whole wheat flour
- Add extra 25g water for absorption
- Expect denser, more complex flavor

### Extended Flavor Development

- Cold retard shaped dough up to 48 hours
- Use mature starter (unfed for 24+ hours)
- Lower hydration (350g water) for more concentrated flavor

### Higher Hydration

- Increase water to 400g for more open crumb
- Requires confident handling and shaping skills
- Expect stickier dough and longer bulk fermentation

---

## Baker's Notes

This recipe represents the foundation of traditional sourdough baking. Master this basic formula before experimenting with additions or variations. The key to consistent results is understanding your starter's rhythm and reading the dough's signals rather than strictly following timing.

Remember: sourdough is forgiving. Each loaf teaches you something new about fermentation, timing, and technique. Keep detailed notes on temperature, timing, and results to improve your next bake.

9. 5 Add cooked linguine to skillet. Toss pasta in sauce over low heat until noodles have absorbed some (not

# Whole Baked Fish – Herb-stuffed with Garlic & Dill Butter Sauce

Whole Baked Fish – Herb-stuffed with Garlic & Dill Butter Sauce - RecipeTin Eats

## Overview
- **Cook Time**: 10 mins 20 mins
- **Servings**: 4 Calories

## Ingredients
- 2 x 800g / 1.6 lb whole snapper or other whole fish , scaled, gutted and cleaned (Note 1)
- 1 1/2 tsp salt , kosher/cooking (not table salt)
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil
- Stuffing:
- 1/2 cup fresh dill sprigs, packed
- 1/2 cup parsley leaves, packed
- 4 garlic cloves , finely sliced
- 1 lemon , sliced (8 slices each lemon)
- Dill Garlic Butter:
- 150g / 10 tbsp unsalted butter , cut into cubes
- 2 tsp garlic , finely minced
- 1 tbsp fresh dill , finely chopped

## Instructions
1. Preheat oven to 220°C/430°F (200°C fan). Line a tray with parchment/baking paper.
2. Trim fins: Cut all fins off the fish using scissors – both fins on the side, and the fins on the
3. back and underside of the fish (but not the tail).
3. Slash flesh: Cut 3 slashes on each side of the fish, cutting through flesh down to the bone
4. (see photos in post and/or video, helpful!).
5. Whole Baked Fish – Herb-stuffed with Garlic & Dill Butter Sauce - RecipeTin Eats
4. Stuff fish (Note 2): Sprinkle a bit of salt and pepper inside the cavity of the fish. Scatter the
5. cavity with garlic slices, then stuff with parsley and dill. Layer lemons on top of herbs.
5. Tie fish (Note 3): Using kitchen string make 3 ties to hold fish together.
6. Season skin: Sprinkle remaining salt and pepper on the skin (both sides), including a bit on
7. the head of the fish. Then drizzle with olive oil. Rub all over the fish, including in the slashes.
7. Bake 20 minutes (Note 4): Place fish on prepared tray. Bake for 20 minutes or until the
8. internal temperature is 55°C/131°F (insert thermometer in the thickest part of the fish, not
9. against the bone). Alternatively, use a small knife at one of the cut slits in the fish to prise a
10. bit of meat gently away from the spine. If it flakes away from the bone without resistance, it's
11. done.
8. Rest: Remove from oven, transfer to serving platter and leave it to rest for 5 minutes. The
9. internal temperature will rise to 58°C / 136.5F ("medium", ie. just-cooked and not raw at all,
10. very juicy and moist).
9. Serve with Garlic & Dill Butter Sauce on the side. Either pour over the butter just prior to

## Notes
1. Fish - I've used snapper here but this recipe is suitable for many types of fish.
For this recipe I would recommend mostly sticking round fish. These are fish that are shaped like
the snapper pictured in this post. They are roughly cylindrical in the centre of their bodies, and
swim upright (as contrasted with say flat fish like flounder, turbot, sole etc that swim lying flat).
Round fish fillets tend to be thicker, making them easier to cook.
I would also recommend fish with large and flat fillets such as the snapper pictured. This is for ease
of stuffing, for better flesh yield, easier cooking and also for serving. Torpedo-shaped fish like
flathead, gurnard / latchet and catfish, or fish with very large heads like rock cod, will be a slightly
more challenging.
Avoid: fish that tend to dry out easily as kingfish, tuna, mackerel, or bonito.
Suggested fish that are suitably sized and shaped for cooking whole:
Snapper (pictured)
Bream / dorade
Barramundi
Blue cod / blue eye trevalla
Jewfish / mulloway
 2/3
 Whole Baked Fish – Herb-stuffed with Garlic & Dill Butter Sauce - RecipeTin Eats
Trout (river)
Salmon (small ones)
Cod
Haddock
Bass / sea bass / branzino
Pollock
Tilapia
2. Cavity of fish – This is the empty belly area where the guts were.
3. Tying fish – This step is recommended but not essential. It holds the fish together so the flavour
from the herbs etc infuses into the flesh better, and holds the fish in shape (stops the belly flaps
from curling outwards). Do not worry about doing fancy butcher-style tying with a single piece of
string. Just get three string lengths, and tie them around the fish at intervals! It does the same job.
4. Cooking time for whole fish – 20 minutes is for 800g individual fish (any number). Larger fish
will take longer to cook, and different shaped fish can take slightly different cooking times. It is not
an exact science, so start checking your fish at the 15 minute mark and every few minutes from
there.

# Wild mushroom soup - Hotel Rangá

Wild mushroom soup - Hotel Rangá

## Overview
- **Total Time**: 2 hrs
- **Servings**: 4 people

## Ingredients
- 400 g Icelandic mushrooms or fresh field mushrooms
- 2 White onions
- 100 g Dried mushrooms
- 200 g Mixed frozen mushrooms ceps, porcini or similar
- 5 tbsp Vegetable oil
- 300 g Butter
- 100 g Plain white flour
- 100 ml White wine
- 100 ml Madeira
- 500 ml Water
- 2 L Double or heavy cream
- 3 tbsp Mushroom powder

## Instructions
1. Method
2. Wild mushroom soup - Hotel Rangá
1. Slice the mushrooms and onions thinly.
2. Take a large heavy-based saucepan and gently heat the oil.
3. Gently fry the fresh mushrooms, onions and frozen mushrooms for 5 min.
4. Pour all the wine into the pan and let it boil until the wine has reduced to almost nothing.
5. Add the water to the pan.
6. Now add the dried mushrooms and stir.
7. Add the mushroom powder into the pan and let the mixture boil for 20 min.
8. Now add the cream into the pot and let it simmer for 60 min.
9. In a small pan place 100 g of butter, heat gently and let it melt, then add flour into it and combine it together to make a roux.
10. Whisk the roux mixture into the soup and continue whisking until the soup thickens.
10. Let the soup simmer for 10 min and then add the remaining 200 g of the butter.
11. Blitz the soup with a hand-held blender.
12. Season with salt and pepper, also it is very good to add a little bit of sherry vinegar at the end.

# Wonton Soup

Recipe VIDEO above. Homemade wontons are amazing! No fillers, just real

## Overview
- **Total Time**: 20 mins 15 mins 35 mins
- **Servings**: 50 wontons

## Ingredients
- 50 - 60 wonton wrappers (Note 1)
- Wonton Filling
- 200 g / 7 oz lean pork mince (ground pork)
- 200 g / 7 oz peeled prawns / shrimp , roughly chopped
- 1 tbsp ginger , finely grated (1.5" / 3cm piece)
- 2 shallots / green onions , finely chopped (5 tbsp)
- 1 tbsp light soy sauce (Note 2)
- 2 tbsp Chinese cooking wine (Shaoxing wine) (Note 3)
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 2 tbsp sesame oil, toasted (Note 4)
- Broth (for 2 servings)
- 3 cups / 750 ml chicken broth (Note 5)
- 2 garlic cloves , smashed (6)
- ⅓" / 1 cm piece of ginger , sliced (optional, but highly recommended)
- 1½ tbsp light soy sauce (Note 2)
- 2 tsp sugar (any)
- 1½ tbsp chinese cooking wine (Note 3)
- ¼ - ½ tsp sesame oil
- To Serve
- 1/4
- Wonton Soup - RecipeTin Eats
- Shallots / scallions , finely chopped
- Bok choy , quartered, or Chinese broccoli cut into 10cm /4" lengths (optional)
- 40 - 50 g / 1.5 - 1.75 oz dried egg noodles per person , (optional) (8)

## Instructions
1. Wontons:
1. Place Filling ingredients in a bowl. Use a potato masher to mash until fairly smooth - about 20
2. mashes. Don't turn the prawn into a complete paste, small chunks are good.
3. Wrapping (See photos and video):
1. Use My Way (better Wonton Soup experience!) or the Asian Grocery Store Way (easier to pack
2. for freezing).
2. Lay Wontons on work surface. Use 2 teaspoons to put the Filling on the wontons. Work in
3. batches of 5 if starting out, up to 15 or 20 if confident. Brush 2 edges with water. Fold to seal,
4. pressing out air. Brush water on one corner and bring corners together, pressing to seal.
3. Place wrapped wontons into a container with a lid as you work (so they don't dry out).
4. Cooking/Freezing:
1. To cook: bring a large pot of water to boil. Place wontons in water and cook for 4 minutes or
2. until they float. Remove with slotted spoon straight into serving bowls. Ladle over broth.
2. To freeze: Freeze uncooked in airtight containers. Cook from frozen for 6 to 8 minutes.
3. IMPORTANT: Do not freeze if you made this with defrosted frozen prawns. (Note 11)
4. Broth:
1. Place Broth ingredients in a saucepan over high heat. Add white ends of scallions/shallots if
2. leftover from Wonton filling.
2. Place lid on, bring to simmer then reduce to medium high and simmer for 5 - 10 minutes to
3. allow the flavours to infuse. Pick garlic and ginger out before using.
3. If using vegetables, blanch in the soup broth and place in serving bowl.
4. Assemble Soup:
1. Prepare noodles according to packet directions (if using noodles). Place in serving bowl with
2. cooked wontons and blanched vegetables.
2. Ladle over soup. Serve!
3. Wonton Soup - RecipeTin Eats

## Notes
1. Wonton Wrappers - You can find Wonton Wrappers in the refrigerator section of Woolworths
and Coles in Australia in the section where fresh noodles are sold (usually next to the pasta). You
will need 2 packets (there are 40 in each pack). Or otherwise reduce the filling slightly and just
make 1 packet.
2. Soy Sauce - You can sub with 1 tbsp + 1 tsp all purpose soy sauce. Read more about different
types of soy sauce here.
3. Chinese cooking wine (Shaoxing wine) - I highly recommend using Chinese cooking wine per
recipe as it adds depth of flavour into the filling. Sub with sherry, cooking sake or Mirin. If you
cannot consume alcohol, then just omit.
4. Sesame Oil - This sounds like a lot, but trust me, it tastes incredible! Use toasted (brown oil) for
better flavour, not untested (yellow).
5. Chicken broth - If you are at the Asian store, grab a couple of cans of Asian chicken broth. It's
more yellow and tastes a little "cleaner" than Western store bought chicken broth. It is what I used
in the photos.
6. Smash garlic cloves by pressing the side of the knife down on the side so they burst open but
mostly stay whole. It allows the flavour to infuse into the soup while making it easy to pick out of
the broth before serving so you have a clean broth without bits of garlic in it.
7. I use 6 to 8 wontons for soups without noodles, and 5 or 6 with noodles.
8. I use these Asian egg noodles from Woolworths in Australia. Any dried or fresh egg noodles will
work fine.
9. When I'm feeling really lazy, I cook the wontons in the soup broth. Just be aware that it will suck
up some of the broth so add 1/2 cup of water.
10. The filling for the wontons are from this Wonton Soup recipe by Omnivore's Cookbook, a
fantastic authentic Chinese food blog. It is better than my mother's!!
11. IMPORTANT: Do not freeze if you make this with prawn meat that was frozen - you should
not refreeze raw seafood. Use all pork. Or if you really have to have prawns in your wontons, cook
them very lightly in a skillet until they are JUST cooked (still opaque, not solid white), then chop
 3/4
 Wonton Soup - RecipeTin Eats
them finely with a knife (i.e. almost mince them). Mash up the pork per recipe, then at the end just
stir the prawns in - scrape any juices on cutting board in as well.
12. Nutrition per serving, with bok choy, no noodles. If you add egg noodles, it increases to 347
calories per serving. Make it even healthier by adding more vegetables - just blanch them in the
soup broth.
